They crossed the river, but when they reached the other side, the old man wiped his hands and walked away. Timmy felt betrayed and he started to cry. He had learnt a valuable lesson that day. Life can be harsh and you should always be humble.

Ben told them what he did. He said he was sorry. He asked them to help him get out.

They nodded. They worked together and gently pulled the bee ball. They were careful not to hurt Ben. After a while, they managed to get him out. He was free. He was happy.

They hugged him and kissed him. They told him they loved him. They also told him to be careful and not to do that again.

Ben nodded. He thanked them. He also thanked Lily. He said he was sorry for taking the bee ball and getting stuck. He said he learned his lesson.

Lily smiled. She forgave him. She said she was glad he was okay. She said they could still play with the bee ball, but only the right way.

They agreed. They put the bee ball back in the box. They were organized. They played with their other toys. They were happy. They were friends.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of being careful, sharing, and learning from mistakes.

Sara liked to mail letters to her grandma. She would draw pictures of flowers and animals and write her name with big letters. She would put the letters in envelopes and stick stamps on them. Then she would ask her mom to take her to the mailbox.

One day, Sara found a beetle in the garden. It was shiny and black and had six legs. Sara thought it was pretty and wanted to show it to her grandma. She decided to mail the beetle to her grandma. She put the beetle in a small box and made holes in it. She wrote "To Grandma" on the box and put a stamp on it. She asked her mom to take her to the mailbox.

"Mom, can we mail this box to grandma?" Sara asked.

"What's in the box, Sara?" her mom asked.

"A beetle. I found it in the garden. I want to share it with grandma. She likes bugs," Sara said.

"Sara, you can't mail a beetle to grandma. It's not nice to the beetle. It needs air and water and food. It will be sad and scared in the box. And grandma might not like to get a beetle in the mail. She might be sad and scared too," her mom said.

Sara looked at the box and felt sad. She didn't want to hurt the beetle or make grandma unhappy. She wanted to do something nice for them.

"Can I keep the beetle as a pet, mom?" Sara asked.

"No, Sara. The beetle belongs in the garden. It has a home and a family there. It will be happy there. You can visit it sometimes, but you have to let it go," her mom said.

Sara nodded. She opened the box and took out the beetle. She held it gently in her hand and said goodbye to it. She put it back in the garden and watched it crawl away.

"Bye, beetle. I hope you have a good life. Maybe I'll see you again," Sara said.

She felt a little better. She still wanted to mail something to grandma. She thought for a moment and then smiled. She had an idea.

"Mom, can I mail a picture of the beetle to grandma?" Sara asked.

"Yes, Sara. That's a great idea. Grandma will love to see your picture of the beetle. She will be happy and proud of you," her mom said.

Sara ran inside and got her crayons and paper. She drew a picture of the beetle and wrote "I love you, grandma" on it. She put it in an envelope and stuck a stamp on it. She asked her mom to take her to the mailbox.

Sara mailed her picture to grandma. She felt happy. She hoped grandma would like it. She hoped the beetle would like it too.

Tommy had a furry toy bear that he loved very much. He called him Glow Bear, because he had a button on his tummy that made him glow in the dark. Tommy liked to hug Glow Bear when he went to bed, and Glow Bear liked to keep Tommy warm and safe.

One night, Tommy heard a noise outside his window. He was scared and held Glow Bear tight. He pressed the button and Glow Bear lit up like a star. Tommy saw a big shadow on the wall. It looked like a monster with horns and teeth. Tommy screamed and hid under the covers.

"Grrr! Who are you?" the shadow said. "Why are you glowing?"

Tommy peeked out and saw that the shadow was not a monster, but a goat. The goat had climbed on the roof and was looking through the window. He was curious about the glowing toy.

"I'm Tommy, and this is Glow Bear," Tommy said. "He is my furry friend and he glows because he has a magic button."

"A magic button?" the goat said. "Can I see it?"

Tommy was brave and showed the goat the button. The goat sniffed it and tried to bite it.

"Hey, stop that!" Tommy said. "You'll break it!"

"Sorry, sorry," the goat said. "I thought it was food. It smells good."

"Well, it's not food, it's Glow Bear's button. He needs it to glow and make me happy. He is my owner and I am his owner. We belong to each other."

The goat nodded and smiled. He understood. He had an owner too, a farmer who gave him hay and water and a bell. He liked his owner and his owner liked him.

Tommy smiled and nodded. He liked the goat. He was not a monster, he was just lonely.

"Sure, you can be our friend," Tommy said. "But you have to be careful with Glow Bear's button. And you have to go back to your owner in the morning. He will miss you."

"OK, OK," the goat said. "I will go back. But can I stay with you tonight? It's cold and dark outside."

Tommy agreed and made room for the goat on his bed. He hugged Glow Bear and the goat hugged him. They all glowed together and fell asleep. They were happy. They were friends.

"Oh no!" Anna says. "Where is the ball?"

Ben runs after the ball. He looks in the snow. He sees a small hole. He puts his hand in the hole. He feels something round and furry.

"Ouch!" Ben says. He pulls his hand out. He has a scratch on his finger. He sees a mouse with the ball in its mouth. The mouse runs away.

"Look, Anna!" Ben says. "A mouse took our ball!"

Anna comes to see. She laughs. She sees the mouse and the ball. The mouse looks happy.

"Maybe the mouse likes soccer too," Anna says. "Let's make a new ball with the snow."

Anna and Ben make a snowball. They play soccer with the snowball. They have fun. They are not cold anymore. They are happy.

Lily thought that was a good idea. She took her red ink and her blue ink and poured them into a cup. She stirred them with a spoon. She saw that the ink turned purple. She was very happy. She said, "Thank you, mom, you are very smart. Now I can finish my rainbow."

Ben looked at the worm and said, "Wow, that's a big worm! Can I hold it?"

Lily smiled too and said, "Me too. Let's find more worms."

They ran back to the dirt and dug some more. They found more worms and put them in a bucket. They were having fun.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was the water from the hose. Their mom was watering the flowers. The water was coming fast and strong. It was going to the drain.

Lily and Ben saw the water and the drain. They got scared. They thought the water would take their worms to the drain. They didn't want to lose their worms. They loved their worms.

They ran to the bucket and grabbed it. They tried to move it away from the water and the drain. But the bucket was heavy and they were small. They couldn't lift it. They started to cry.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the bucket, the worms, the water and the drain. She understood what they were trying to do. She felt sorry for them. She said, "Don't cry, Lily and Ben. I'll help you. I'll turn off the water and move the bucket. Your worms are safe. They won't go to the drain."

She did what she said. She turned off the water and moved the bucket. She hugged Lily and Ben and said, "You are very kind and caring. You love your worms and you want to protect them. That's very charming. But you also have to be careful. Water can be dangerous. It can hurt you and your worms. You have to stay away from the water and the drain. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We understand. Thank you for helping us. We're sorry for making a mess."

Their mom smiled and said, "It's okay. I'm glad you're safe. And I'm proud of you for being charming. Now, let's go inside and wash your hands. Then you can play with your worms some more. But only in a safe place. Okay?"

Lily and Ben said, "Okay, mom. We love you."

Sammy was grateful to Finn for saving him. Finn realized that being a good friend was more important than being the biggest or brightest fish in the ocean. From then on, Finn was happy just being himself and being a good friend to all the fish in the ocean.

So, every day, Timmy would look for pennies and put them in his piggy bank. As his piggy bank filled up, Timmy became happy and proud. He knew that one day he would have enough green money to buy anything he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat oranges and play with her toys. One day, she accidentally broke her favorite toy car. She was sad and didn't know what to do.

Her mom saw her sad face and asked, "What happened, Lily?"

"I broke my car," Lily said with a frown.

"It's okay, I can fix it for you," her mom said kindly.

But Lily didn't want to wait for her mom to fix it. She tried to fix it herself, but she made it worse. The car was now broken beyond repair. Lily felt even sadder.

The moral of the story is that sometimes it's better to ask for help instead of trying to fix things ourselves.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, even when it was cold. One day, she went outside to play and it was very chilly. She started to shiver because she didn't have a warm coat on.

As her mom was knitting, Lily asked, "Mommy, why do we need sweaters?" Her mom replied, "We need sweaters to keep us warm when it's cold outside. Just like how your sweater is keeping you warm right now." Lily smiled and hugged her mom, feeling grateful for her new cozy sweater.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with toys. Tom has a big helicopter. It can fly and make noise. Sam has a small car. It can run and beep.

One day, Tom and Sam go to the park. They see a rich man. He has a real helicopter. It is shiny and loud. The rich man lands the helicopter on the grass. He gets out and walks away.

Tom and Sam run to the helicopter. They want to see it. They touch it and look inside. They pretend to fly it.

"Let me sit in the pilot seat," Tom says. He pushes Sam.

"No, let me sit in the pilot seat," Sam says. He pushes Tom back.

They quarrel. They pull and shout. They do not share.

The rich man comes back. He sees Tom and Sam. He is angry.

"Hey, what are you doing? Get away from my helicopter!" he yells.

Tom and Sam are scared. They run away. They drop their toys.

The rich man picks up the toys. He throws them in the trash.

Tom and Sam are sad. They lose their toys. They cry.

They look at each other. They are sorry.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I should have shared with you," Sam says.

"I'm sorry, Sam. I should have shared with you, too," Tom says.

They hug. They are friends again.

They go home. They tell their moms what happened. Their moms are proud of them. They give them new toys. Tom gets a new car. Sam gets a new helicopter.

They play with their new toys. They share. They are happy.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing and slide and run. They saw a big rat near the trash can. The rat was brown and dirty and had sharp teeth.

"Look, a rat!" Tim said. "Let's chase it away!"

"No, Tim, don't!" Lily said. "The rat is scared and hungry. Maybe it has no home or friends. It suffers a lot."

"But rats are bad and mean. They bite and steal and make noise," Tim said.

"Not all rats are bad and mean. Some rats are nice and smart. They can learn and help and play," Lily said. "Maybe this rat is lonely and needs a friend. We can be generous and share some of our snacks with it."

Lily took out a piece of cheese from her backpack. She broke it in half and gave one half to Tim. She walked slowly to the rat and held out the other half. The rat sniffed the cheese and looked at Lily. It saw that Lily was kind and gentle. It took the cheese from her hand and ate it. It squeaked happily and rubbed its nose against Lily's finger.

"Wow, you made friends with the rat!" Tim said. "Can I try too?"

"Sure, Tim. Be careful and quiet. Don't scare the rat," Lily said.

Tim gave his half of the cheese to the rat. The rat took it and ate it. It squeaked again and rubbed its nose against Tim's finger. Tim and Lily smiled and laughed. They had a new friend. The rat was happy and grateful. It did not suffer anymore.

Sara and Ben liked to look at the stars at night. They wondered what was out there in the sky. One night, they saw a bright light moving fast. They thought it was a star, but it was not. It was a spaceship.

The spaceship landed in their backyard. A door opened and a green man came out. He had big eyes and a long nose. He looked at Sara and Ben and said something in a strange language. Sara and Ben were scared, but curious. They asked him who he was and where he came from.

The green man pointed to the sky and said, "I come from planet Zog. I am looking for friends. Do you want to be my friends?" Sara and Ben nodded. They wanted to see his planet and learn more about him. They thought he was lonely and poor.

The green man smiled and said, "Come with me. I will show you my planet. It is very beautiful and fun. You will like it there." He took their hands and led them to his spaceship. He closed the door and pushed a button. The spaceship took off and flew away.

Sara and Ben did not know that the green man was lying. He was not looking for friends. He was looking for food. He was hungry and greedy. His planet was not beautiful and fun. It was dark and cold. He did not like it there. He wanted to eat Sara and Ben. He had a big pot and a fire in his spaceship. He was going to cook them and eat them. Sara and Ben were in big trouble. They tried to scream and escape, but it was too late. The green man did not reply. He only laughed. Sara and Ben were very sad and afraid. They wished they had never met the green man. They wished they had stayed at home. They wished they had listened to their mom, who always told them not to talk to strangers. But it was too late. The end.

One day, she found a new car in her toy box. It was shiny and red, with a big fuel tank on the back. It looked very fast and strong. Lily was curious and excited. She picked up the car and made it zoom on the floor.

But something was wrong. The car did not zoom very far. It stopped after a few seconds. Lily tried again, but the car did not move. She looked at the fuel tank. It was empty. The car had no fuel.

Lily was sad and confused. She wanted to play with the new car, but it did not work. She wondered where she could find some fuel. She looked around the room, but she did not see anything that looked like fuel.

Then she had an idea. She remembered that her daddy had a big bottle of water in the kitchen. She thought that maybe water could be fuel for the car. She ran to the kitchen and grabbed the bottle. She poured some water into the fuel tank of the car. She hoped it would work.

She took the car back to the floor and made it zoom. To her delight, the car zoomed very fast and far. It zoomed all over the room, making Lily laugh and clap. She was so happy that she had fixed the car. She thought the car was adorable and clever. She decided to name it Zoomy. She hugged Zoomy and played with him all day.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play ball. They had a big ball that was red and blue and bounced high. They liked to throw the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they threw the ball very hard and far. They called this a pitch.

One day, they decided to test who could pitch the ball the farthest. They went to the park and found a big space. They took turns to pitch the ball and see how far it went. Tim pitched the ball first. He threw it very hard and it flew far away. Sam said, "Wow, that was a good pitch!"

Then Sam pitched the ball. He threw it even harder and it flew even farther. Tim said, "Wow, that was a better pitch!"

They kept pitching the ball and trying to beat each other. They did not see the other people in the park. They did not see the old man walking his dog. They did not see the little girl riding her bike. They did not see the big tree.

The last time Sam pitched the ball, he threw it so hard that it hit the old man's dog. The dog yelped and ran away. The old man shouted, "Hey, what are you doing? You hurt my dog!"

The last time Tim pitched the ball, he threw it so hard that it hit the little girl's bike. The bike wobbled and fell over. The little girl cried and scraped her knee. The little girl's mom yelled, "Hey, what are you doing? You hurt my daughter!"

The last time the ball came back, it hit the big tree. The tree shook and dropped a big branch. The branch fell on Tim and Sam and knocked them down. They groaned and felt pain. The branch was heavy and they could not get up.

The old man, the little girl, and her mom came to see what happened. They saw Tim and Sam under the branch. They were angry and scared. They said, "You are bad boys! You should not pitch the ball so hard and hurt people and animals and trees! You should be sorry and say sorry!"

But Tim and Sam did not say sorry. They were too proud and stubborn. They said, "We were just testing who could pitch the ball the farthest. We did not mean to hurt anyone or anything. It was just an ordinary game!"

The old man, the little girl, and her mom did not believe them. They did not think it was an ordinary game. They thought it was a dangerous and rude game. They called the police and the ambulance. The police and the ambulance came and took Tim and Sam away. They were in trouble and had to pay for the damage and the injuries. They lost their ball and their friendship. They were sad and sorry, but it was too late.

Mia and Leo liked to play in the park. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. They also liked to watch the birds and the bugs. Mia wanted to catch a fly, but Leo said it was too hard.

"I can do it," Mia said. "I am independent. I don't need your help."

She ran after a big green fly. She tried to grab it with her hand, but it flew away. She tried to catch it with her hat, but it escaped. She tried to trap it with her net, but it dodged. Mia was getting tired and angry.

"Give up, Mia," Leo said. "You can't catch a fly. They are too fast and smart."

"No, I won't give up," Mia said. "I have a plan. I will reveal my secret weapon."

She took out a jar from her backpack. Inside the jar, there was something shiny and sticky. It was honey. Mia opened the jar and put it on the ground. She hid behind a tree and waited.

The fly smelled the honey. It flew towards the jar. It landed on the edge and licked the honey. It was sweet and yummy. The fly wanted more. It crawled inside the jar. But then, it got stuck. The honey was too sticky. The fly could not fly away.

Mia jumped out from behind the tree. She ran to the jar and closed the lid. She caught the fly. She was happy and proud.

"Look, Leo, I did it!" Mia said. "I caught a fly with my secret weapon. I am independent. I don't need your help."

Leo was surprised and impressed. He clapped his hands and smiled.

"Wow, Mia, you are clever and brave," Leo said. "You caught a fly with your secret weapon. You are independent. But you are also my friend. Can I see your fly?"

Mia nodded and showed him the jar. The fly was buzzing and trying to get out. Mia felt sorry for the fly. She realized that the fly was independent too. It wanted to be free.

"Maybe we should let the fly go," Mia said. "It is not nice to keep it in a jar. It wants to fly and play."

Leo agreed. He said it was kind and fair. They opened the jar and let the fly go. The fly flew away and thanked them. Mia and Leo waved goodbye and hugged. They were independent, but they were also friends. They went back to play in the park. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. They also liked to watch the birds and the bugs. But they did not try to catch them anymore.

Tom was a little boy who liked to learn new things. He liked to look at books, play with toys, and ask questions. One day, he saw a big storm in the sky. He heard loud noises and saw bright flashes. He was scared and ran to his mom.

Mom hugged Tom and said, "Don't be scared, Tom. That is lightning and thunder. They are part of the storm. Lightning is when electricity moves in the sky. Thunder is when the air makes a noise. They can't hurt you if you are inside."

Tom looked at his mom and said, "Why is lightning red sometimes?"

Mom smiled and said, "Lightning can be different colors, depending on what is in the air. Sometimes it is white, sometimes it is yellow, sometimes it is blue, and sometimes it is red. Red lightning is rare and special. It means there is a lot of dust or smoke in the air."

Tom nodded and said, "I see. I learned something new today. Thank you, mom."

Mom kissed Tom and said, "You're welcome, Tom. I'm glad you like to learn. Learning is fun and good for you. Now, let's watch the storm together and see if we can spot more red lightning."

Lila and Sam liked to play in the river. They had a big raft that they made with wood and rope. They put their toys and snacks on the raft and floated along the water.

One day, they saw a new boy on the shore. He had a small raft that he made with a tire and a stick. He waved at them and said, "Hi, I'm Max. Can I join you?"

Lila and Sam smiled and said, "Sure, come on." They helped Max tie his raft to theirs and they shared their toys and snacks. They had fun playing and talking.

But soon, Max became bossy. He wanted to steer the raft and decide where to go. He said, "I'm the captain of this raft. You have to do what I say."

Lila and Sam did not like that. They said, "No, you're not. We made this raft together. We can all take turns and be nice."

Max did not listen. He said, "No, I'm the captain and you're the crew. You have to obey me or you can leave."

Lila and Sam were angry and sad. They said, "Fine, we'll leave. We don't want to play with you anymore." They untied their raft from Max's and floated away.

Max was left alone on his small raft. He felt lonely and sorry. He realized he was wrong and he had no friends. He wished he had been nicer to Lila and Sam. He called out, "Wait, come back. I'm sorry. Can we be friends again?"

But Lila and Sam did not hear him. They were too far away. They found a new spot to play and had fun without him. They hoped Max would learn to be kind and share.

Lily was a young girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna, who had long hair and a pretty dress. Lily liked to wash Anna's hair and make it shiny and soft.

One day, Lily's grandpa came to visit. He was old and walked with a cane. He smiled at Lily and said, "Hello, my dear. What are you doing?"

"I'm washing Anna's hair," Lily said. "She likes it when I do that."

Grandpa was hurt by Lily's words. He loved Lily and wanted to play with her. He said, "Lily, don't be rude. I just wanted to look at your doll. I'm sorry if I upset you."

Grandpa smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a sweet girl. I'm glad you like your doll. Maybe we can play together later."

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, Grandpa. I would like that. But first, I have to dry Anna's hair."

Grandpa and Lily laughed and went to find a towel. They dried Anna's hair and made it shiny and soft. Then they played with the other dolls and had fun. Lily was happy and Grandpa was happy. They loved each other very much.

Penny was a little penguin who loved to swim and play in the snow. She was very graceful and fast in the water, and she could slide on her belly on the ice. She had many friends who liked to swim and play with her, but she also liked to sleep a lot. Sometimes, she would sleep so much that she would miss the fun with her friends.

One day, she was sleeping on a big rock, when she heard a loud noise. She opened her eyes and saw a big seal coming towards her. She was scared and tried to run away, but the seal was faster and caught her by the tail. Penny cried for help, but no one heard her.

Then, she saw Ben, her best friend, who was swimming nearby. He saw Penny in trouble and quickly swam to her. He bit the seal's nose and made him let go of Penny. Penny was free and swam to Ben. They hugged and thanked each other.

"Are you okay, Penny?" Ben asked.

"Yes, thank you, Ben. You saved me!" Penny said.

"You're welcome, Penny. But why were you sleeping on the rock? Didn't you hear the seal coming?" Ben asked.

"I was too tired, Ben. I sleep a lot, you know. I like to sleep." Penny said.

"I know, Penny, but sleeping too much is not good for you. You need to be alert and careful, especially when there are seals around. And you also miss the fun with your friends when you sleep too much. Don't you want to swim and play with us?" Ben asked.

"I do, Ben, I do. But I also like to sleep." Penny said.

"Penny, sleeping is good, but not too much. You need to find a balance. You need to sleep when it's dark and wake up when it's light. You need to sleep enough, but not too much. You need to sleep to rest, but not to miss life. Do you understand, Penny?" Ben asked.

"I think I do, Ben. Thank you for teaching me. You are a good friend." Penny said.

"You're welcome, Penny. You are a good friend too. Now, let's go and join our friends. They are waiting for us. And don't worry, I'll always watch over you when you sleep." Ben said.

"Okay, Ben. Let's go. And I'll watch over you too when you sleep." Penny said.

They swam away, happy and safe, and joined their friends. Penny learned a valuable lesson that day. She learned to sleep enough, but not too much. She learned to be alert and careful, but also to have fun. She learned to find a balance in life. And she learned to appreciate her friends, especially Ben, who was always there for her.

Sara and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big tree with many leaves. They want to climb the tree and look for birds and bugs. They run to the tree and start to climb.

"Look, Sara, I see a monkey!" Ben says. He points to a brown animal with a long tail. The monkey is sitting on a branch and eating a banana.

"Wow, a monkey! How did it get here?" Sara asks. She climbs closer to Ben and the monkey. The monkey looks at them and makes a funny noise.

"Maybe it escaped from the zoo. It is very attractive. I like its fur and eyes," Ben says. He tries to reach for the monkey. He wants to touch it and make friends.

"Be careful, Ben. The monkey might be scared or angry. It might bite you or scratch you," Sara says. She is worried about Ben. She remembers that her mom told her not to touch wild animals.

But Ben does not listen to Sara. He moves his hand closer to the monkey. The monkey does not like it. It drops its banana and jumps at Ben. It grabs his hair and pulls it hard.

"Ow, ow, ow! Help, Sara, help!" Ben cries. He feels pain and fear. He wants the monkey to let go of his hair.

Sara does not know what to do. She sees a big sign on the tree. It says "Freeze". She thinks it means to stop moving. She hopes the monkey will stop too. She shouts to Ben.

"Ben, freeze! Don't move! Maybe the monkey will stop if we freeze!"

Ben hears Sara. He stops moving. He freezes. He hopes Sara is right. He hopes the monkey will stop.

The monkey sees that Ben and Sara are not moving. It thinks they are playing a game. It likes games. It lets go of Ben's hair. It makes a happy noise. It jumps to another branch and looks for another banana.

Ben and Sara are relieved. They are glad the monkey is gone. They are not hurt, but they are scared. They decide to climb down the tree and go back to their mom. They learn their lesson. They do not touch wild animals. They only look at them from far away.

Tom looked around the room and tried to find Lily. He saw the bed, the closet, the toys, but no Lily. He wondered where she was. He called out, "Lily, where are you? I can't find you. Come out, come out, wherever you are!"

Lily heard Tom's voice and giggled. She thought she was very clever and Tom would never find her. She stayed behind the lamp and did not answer. She wanted to win the game.

But then, something bad happened. The lamp was not very stable and Lily's movement made it wobble. The lamp fell over and crashed on the floor. It broke into many pieces and made a loud noise. Lily was scared and cried out, "Help, help, I'm here!"

Tom heard Lily's cry and ran to the corner. He saw the broken lamp and Lily behind it. He was worried and angry. He said, "Lily, what did you do? You broke the lamp. That was very naughty. You should not hide behind things that can break. You could have hurt yourself or made a fire. You should have answered me when I called you. That was not a good game."

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I wanted to hide well and win the game. I did not mean to break the lamp. I did not think it would fall. I was afraid to answer you because I thought you would find me. I was not a good hider. I was a bad sister."

Tom hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you are not hurt. But you should be more careful and listen to me when I call you. Hiding is fun, but not when it is dangerous or rude. We should play fair and safe. We should be good to each other. We are brother and sister. We love each other."

Lily nodded and said, "I love you, Tom. I'm sorry, again. Can we play another game? A nice game?"

Tom smiled and said, "Sure, Lily. Let's play another game. A nice game. But first, let's clean up the mess and tell Mom and Dad what happened. They might be mad, but they will forgive us. They love us, too."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of honesty, responsibility, safety, and love. It shows that hiding can be fun, but not when it is harmful or disrespectful. It shows that calling and answering are important ways of communicating and caring. It shows that breaking things is wrong and should be admitted and fixed. It shows that siblings should be kind and supportive of each other. It shows that family is important and loving.

"Did you hear that?" Lily asked.

"Stop what?" Lily asked.

"Run!" the chicken said. "Run to the house!"

Jill felt sorry for the old man. She ran to him and helped him up. She said, "I'm sorry, sir. My brother is naughty. He took your cane. I will get it back for you."

She ran after Jack, who was laughing and swinging the cane. She said, "Jack, stop! Give the cane back to the old man. You hurt him. You are mean."

Jack said, "No, Jill, this is my cane now. It is fun. It is mine."

Jill was angry and brave. She grabbed the cane from Jack and pulled it hard. Jack fell and dropped the cane. Jill picked it up and ran back to the old man. She said, "Here, sir, this is your cane. I'm sorry for what my brother did. He is not tough. He is silly."

The old man smiled and thanked Jill. He said, "You are a good girl, Jill. You are kind and honest. You are tough. You are smart."

Jill felt happy and proud. She said, "Thank you, sir. I'm sorry for the trouble. I hope you are okay."

The old man said, "I'm okay, Jill. Don't worry. You and your brother should go home now. And tell your brother to be good. Or else I will use my cane to teach him a lesson."

Jill nodded and took Jack by the hand. She said, "Come on, Jack. Let's go home. And say sorry to the old man."

Jack was ashamed and sorry. He said, "Sorry, sir. I was wrong. I won't steal again."

The old man said, "That's good, Jack. Learn from your sister. She is a good example for you."

Jack and Jill went home and hugged their mom. They told her what happened. Their mom was angry with Jack and proud of Jill. She said, "Jack, you are grounded. You have to stay in your room and think about what you did. Jill, you are a hero. You have to choose a treat from the cookie jar."

Jack and Jill learned a lesson that day. They learned that stealing is bad and helping is good. They learned that being tough is not about being mean, but about being brave and kind. They learned to love and respect each other and other people. They learned to be happy with what they have and not to want what they don't need.

Sara was very scared. She had to go to the hospital and get an x-ray. She hurt her arm when she fell from the swing. She cried and hugged her mom.

"Mom, I don't want to go. It will hurt. I don't like the big machine. It makes a loud noise."

Her mom smiled and kissed her head. She said, "Don't worry, my sweetie. The x-ray will not hurt. It will help the doctor see your arm and make it better. The big machine is just a camera. It takes a picture of your bones. The loud noise is just a beep. It tells us when the picture is done."

Sara looked at her mom. She still felt scared, but she trusted her mom. She said, "Okay, mom. I will try to be brave. But can you hold my hand?"

Her mom nodded and said, "Of course, I will hold your hand. I will be with you all the time. You are not alone. You are very strong and brave. I am proud of you."

They walked to the x-ray room. The nurse was very nice. She gave Sara a sticker and a teddy bear. She said, "Hi, Sara. I am here to help you. You can hold your teddy bear and your mom's hand. I will put a special apron on you to protect you. Then I will ask you to lie down on this table and stay still for a few seconds. That's when the x-ray will take the picture. Can you do that for me?"

Sara nodded. She felt a little better. She said, "Yes, I can do that. Thank you for the sticker and the teddy bear. They are very cute."

The nurse smiled and said, "You are very welcome. You are a very good girl. You are ready for the x-ray. Are you ready to count with me?"

Sara said, "Yes, I am ready to count with you."

The nurse said, "Okay, let's count together. One, two, three, beep!"

Sara heard the beep and saw the flash. She did not move. She did not cry. She did it!

The nurse said, "You did it, Sara! You did a great job! The x-ray is done. You can get up now and hug your mom. The doctor will look at your picture and tell you what to do next. You are very brave and strong. I am proud of you."

Sara got up and hugged her mom. She said, "Mom, I did it! I was not scared. The x-ray was easy. The nurse was nice. The teddy bear was soft. I am brave and strong. I am proud of me."

Her mom hugged her back and said, "I am proud of you, too, Sara. You are brave and strong. You are my hero. I love you."

Sara smiled and said, "I love you, too, mom. Thank you for being with me. Thank you for encouraging me. You are my hero, too."

The moral of the story is: Sometimes we have to do things that scare us, but we can overcome our fears with the help of our loved ones and the people who care for us. They can encourage us and make us feel safe and loved. We are not helpless. We are brave and strong.

"Oh, Lily, what happened?" she asked.

Her mommy looked at the plant and recognized it. It was a venus flytrap, a plant that eats bugs. She had bought it from a shop that sold mysterious plants. She had forgotten to tell Lily not to touch it.

"I'm sorry, Lily, I didn't know you would go near it. It's a venus flytrap, a plant that eats bugs. It bites when it feels something touch it. It's a very mysterious plant. Let me clean your finger and put a band-aid on it. It will be okay soon."

"No, it is mine!" Tim says. He pushes Sam away. Sam falls on the floor and cries.

"Stop it, you two!" Mom says. She hears the noise and comes to the closet. She sees Tim with the flashlight and Sam with tears. She is angry.

"Give the flashlight to Sam, Tim. It is not nice to be selfish. You have to share." Mom says.

But Tim refuses. He shakes his head and runs away. He hides under the bed with the flashlight.

"Tim, come out right now!" Mom says. She follows him to the bedroom. She bends down and looks under the bed. She sees Tim's eyes and the light.

"Please, Mom, let me keep it. It is so cool. I love it." Tim says.

"No, Tim, you have to share. The flashlight is not yours. It belongs to Dad. He needs it for work. You can play with it later, but only if you share with Sam." Mom says.

But Tim still refuses. He turns off the light and crawls deeper under the bed. He does not want to give up the flashlight.

"Fine, Tim, have it your way. But you will be sorry. You will not get any dessert tonight. And you will not watch TV. And you will not play with any other toys. You will stay under the bed until you learn to share." Mom says.

She stands up and walks away. She leaves Tim alone in the dark. Tim feels sad and scared. He wishes he had listened to Mom. He wishes he had shared with Sam. He wishes he had not been selfish. But it is too late. He has no one to play with. He has no fun. He has only the flashlight. And it is not enough.

Lily was a big girl who loved music. She liked to sing and dance and play with her toy piano. She had many songs in her head that made her happy.

One day, she saw a new toy in the store. It was a big drum that made loud noises. Lily wanted the drum very much. She asked her mom to buy it for her, but her mom said no. She said the drum was too big and too noisy and too expensive. She said Lily already had enough toys and she should be happy with what she had.

Lily was very sad and angry. She did not listen to her mom. She threw a tantrum in the store and cried and screamed. She said she hated her mom and her toy piano and her songs. She said she only wanted the big drum.

Her mom was very sad and angry too. She took Lily home and sent her to her room. She said Lily was very naughty and rude and she had to stay in her room until she was sorry.

Lily lay on her bed and sobbed. She felt lonely and bored. She did not have the big drum or any other toy to play with. She did not have any music to make her happy. She wished she had not been so mean to her mom and her toy piano and her songs.

She realized she had made a big mistake. She realized the big drum was not worth losing her mom's love and her own joy. She realized she had been greedy and selfish and ungrateful.

She got up and went to her mom. She hugged her and said she was sorry. She said she loved her mom and her toy piano and her songs. She said she did not need the big drum or any other toy to be happy.

Her mom hugged her back and said she was sorry too. She said she loved Lily and she was proud of her for being a big girl and saying sorry. She said she was happy to see Lily smile and sing and dance and play with her toy piano again.

They went to the living room and made music together. They had fun and laughed and hugged. They were happy with what they had.

The moral of the story is: Be happy with what you have and don't be greedy for what you don't need. Music is more valuable than noise. Love is more important than toys.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play games. They were very competitive and always wanted to win. One day, they found a big book with pictures of animals in their room. They decided to play a game of guessing the names of the animals.

"I go first," said Ben. He opened the book and pointed to a picture of a big gray animal with a long nose and big ears. "What is this?"

Lily looked at the picture and thought hard. She knew the name of the animal, but she wanted to make Ben wait. She pretended to not know and said, "Hmm, I don't know. Is it a mouse?"

Ben laughed and said, "No, silly. It's an elephant. You don't know anything. I win."

Lily felt angry and sad. She wanted to win too. She said, "No fair. You picked an easy one. Let me pick one for you."

She opened the book and pointed to a picture of a small green animal with a shell and four legs. "What is this?"

Ben looked at the picture and thought hard. He did not know the name of the animal. He had never seen it before. He tried to guess and said, "Is it a frog?"

Lily laughed and said, "No, silly. It's a turtle. You don't know anything. I win."

Ben felt angry and sad. He wanted to win too. He said, "No fair. You picked a hard one. Let's play again."

They opened the book and pointed to different pictures of animals. They tried to guess the names of the animals. But they always got them wrong or said them too late. They started to argue and shout at each other. They did not have fun.

Their mom heard them and came to their room. She saw the book and the twins. She said, "What are you doing? Why are you fighting?"

Ben and Lily told their mom about the game and how they wanted to win. Their mom said, "I see. But do you know what the game is really about?"

The twins shook their heads. Their mom said, "The game is not about winning or losing. The game is about learning and sharing. The book has many animals that you don't know. You can learn their names and what they do. You can share what you know and what you don't know. You can help each other and have fun. That's the point of the game."

The twins looked at each other and felt sorry. They realized that their mom was right. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We were wrong. We were too competitive. We want to learn and share and have fun."

Their mom smiled and said, "That's good. I'm proud of you. Now, why don't you pick an animal that you both don't know and try to find out more about it?"

The twins nodded and opened the book. They saw a picture of a big black and white animal with stripes. They said, "What is this?"

Their mom said, "That's a zebra. It's a kind of horse that lives in Africa. It has stripes to hide from predators. Do you want to know more?"

The twins said, "Yes, please. Tell us more."

Their mom said, "Okay. Let me tell you more about the zebra. But first, can you mention another animal that lives in Africa?"

The twins thought for a moment and said, "An elephant!"

Their mom said, "That's right. An elephant lives in Africa too. And do you know what else?"

The twins said, "What else?"

Their mom said, "An elephant and a zebra can be friends. They can help each other and have fun. Just like you and me."

The twins smiled and hugged their mom. They said, "We love you, mom. And we love elephants and zebras too."

The end.

The race started, and Tom and Sam ran as fast as they could. Tom was winning, but then he saw a little cat stuck in a tree. He stopped and helped the cat. Sam won the race, but Tom felt happy. He knew that being a good guard was not just about being fast, but also helping others.

In the end, Tom and Sam became friends. They worked together to plan and keep the big door safe. They learned that being competitive was not as important as being a good friend and a good guard.

After they finished eating, Bob said, "That was good food! Thank you for eating with me, Tim." Tim smiled and said, "You're welcome, Bob! I'm glad we're friends." And so, the slow dog and the little flea continued to be best friends, always helping each other and sharing their food.

She went to school with her backpack and her lunchbox. She saw her teacher and her friends. They said hello and smiled. They went to the classroom and sat at their desks. The teacher gave them the exam papers and pencils. She said, "You have ten minutes to do the exam. Good luck!"

Lily looked at the exam. She saw some words and some numbers and some pictures. She tried to remember what she learned. She wrote her name and started to answer the questions. She knew some of them, but some of them were hard. She thought and thought. She looked at the clock. She only had two minutes left.

She saw a question that asked, "What color is this?" There was a picture of a flower. It was purple. Lily knew that. She liked purple. It was her favorite color. She wrote "purple" on the line. She felt happy. She looked at the next question. It was the last one. It asked, "What are you doing when you bend your legs and touch the floor with your knees?" Lily did not know that. She had never heard that word before. She felt sad. She did not know what to write.

She looked around. She saw her friend Ben. He was sitting next to her. He had finished his exam. He was looking at her. He saw that she was stuck. He whispered, "Psst, Lily, do you need help?" Lily nodded. She whispered, "Yes, please. What is this word?" She pointed at the question. Ben whispered, "That word is kneel. You kneel when you pray or when you play with your toys on the floor. Like this." He showed her how to kneel. Lily whispered, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend." She wrote "kneel" on the line. She felt happy again. She checked her exam. She had answered all the questions. She smiled. She gave her exam to the teacher. She hoped she did well. She went back to her desk and waited for the others. She whispered to Ben, "You are very smart. How did you know that word?" Ben whispered, "My mom taught me. She kneels every night before bed and says thank you to God. She says it is good to be grateful and kind." Lily whispered, "That is nice. Maybe I will try that too." They smiled at each other. They were happy. They had done their best. They were ready for recess.

"Let's go to the temple!" Ben says. "Maybe we can find something fun inside."

"Let's play hide and seek!" Lila says. "You count to ten and I will hide."

"OK, but don't go too far." Ben says. He closes his eyes and starts to count.

Lila runs to find a good hiding spot. She sees a little door that leads to a small room. She thinks it is a good place to hide. She opens the door and goes inside. She closes the door behind her.

But the door is not a real door. It is a trap. As soon as Lila closes it, it locks and she cannot open it again. She hears a loud noise and feels the floor moving. She is scared.

"Ben! Ben! Help me!" She shouts. "I'm in the little room!"

Ben hears Lila's voice. He stops counting and runs to find her. He sees the little door and tries to open it. But it is locked and he cannot open it. He hears the loud noise and feels the floor moving. He is scared too.

"Lila! Lila! I'm here! Don't worry!" He shouts. "I will find a way to get you out!"

He looks around and sees a big lever on the wall. He thinks it might be the key to the trap. He pulls the lever and hopes it will work.

Poppy was a small dog who liked to play with his friends. He had a red ball that he loved very much. He always brought it with him to the park, where he met other dogs and ran around.

One day, he saw a big dog who had a blue ball. Poppy thought the blue ball looked very fun. He wanted to try it. He ran up to the big dog and barked.

"Can I play with your ball?" he asked.

The big dog looked at Poppy and growled. He did not like to share his ball.

"No, you can't. This is my ball. It belongs to me. Go away!" he said.

Poppy felt sad and scared. He ran back to his red ball. He picked it up and hugged it. He was glad he had his own ball. It belonged to him.

But then he heard a loud noise. He looked up and saw the big dog running towards him. He had his blue ball in his mouth. He wanted to take Poppy's red ball too.

"Give me your ball!" he shouted.

Poppy was very afraid. He did not want to lose his red ball. He tried to run away, but the big dog was faster. He caught up with Poppy and bit his tail.

"Ow!" Poppy cried.

He dropped his red ball and the big dog grabbed it. He had both balls now. He laughed and ran away.

Poppy felt very sad and hurt. He had no ball to play with. He felt embarrassed. He wondered if his friends would laugh at him too.

But then he heard a friendly voice. It was his best friend, Daisy. She was a small cat who liked to play with Poppy. She had a yellow ball that she loved very much. She always brought it with her to the park, where she met Poppy and other animals.

"Poppy, are you okay?" she asked.

She saw Poppy's tail and his tears. She felt sorry for him.

"That big dog was very mean. He took your ball. He should not do that. That was your ball. It belonged to you." she said.

She nuzzled Poppy and licked his tail. She made him feel better.

"Here, you can play with my ball. I don't mind. We can share it. It belongs to both of us. We are friends." she said.

She gave Poppy her yellow ball. Poppy smiled and wagged his tail. He was happy again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big tree with many flowers. They wanted to smell the flowers and see if there were bees.

Lily climbed on a branch and reached for a flower. She saw a bee flying out of it. She was not scared. She liked bees. They made honey. Honey was sweet and yummy.

Ben wanted to climb too. He followed Lily on the branch. But he was not careful. He stepped on a weak spot and the branch broke. He fell down with a loud thud.

"Ouch!" he cried. "That hurt!"

Lily looked down and saw Ben on the ground. She was worried. She wanted to help him. But she did not know how to get down. She was stuck on the tree.

"Ben, are you okay?" she called.

"I'm okay, but I'm smelly," he said. "I fell on some mud. And there is something sticky on my head."

Lily saw that Ben had honey on his head. The branch had broken a honeycomb and the honey had spilled on him.

"Ben, you have honey on your head!" she said. "That's why you are smelly. The bees will come and want their honey back."

Ben was scared. He did not like bees anymore. They could sting him. He wanted to get rid of the honey.

"Lily, help me!" he said. "How can I get the honey off?"

Lily thought hard. She had an idea. She saw a bucket near the tree. It had water in it.

"Ben, I have an idea," she said. "See that bucket? It has water. You can use the water to wash the honey off."

Ben saw the bucket. He was happy. He ran to the bucket and dipped his head in it. The water was cold and wet. He rubbed his head and the honey came off.

"Yay, I did it!" he said. "The honey is gone. I'm not smelly anymore."

Lily was happy too. She wanted to get down from the tree. She saw a ladder near the tree. It had been left by the gardener. She used the ladder to get down.

She was careful. She did not want to fall. She balanced on the ladder and climbed down. She reached the ground and hugged Ben.

"Ben, I'm so glad you are okay," she said. "And I'm sorry I made you climb the tree. It was not a good idea."

Ben hugged her back. He was not mad at her. He loved her. She was his sister.

"It's okay, Lily," he said. "It was an adventure. And we learned something. We learned that bees make honey. And that honey is sweet and yummy. But also sticky and smelly. And that we should not touch it."

They laughed and went back to their house. They told their mom what had happened. She was not angry. She was proud. They had been brave and smart. She gave them a hug and a cookie. They ate the cookie and smiled. It was a good day.

Tim wanted to help the angry cat. He opened the garage door wide, and the cat ran out into the yard. The cat was happy now and stopped screaming. Tim felt good because he helped the cat. From that day on, Tim and the cat became best friends, and they played together in the garage every day.

One day, Mom warned Tim, "Do not eat all the chocolate at once or you will get a tummy ache." Tim listened, but he loved chocolate so much. He thought about the chocolate all day.

The next day, Tim went to his room and saw the big box of chocolate. He remembered Mom's warning, but he could not stop thinking about the tasty chocolate. So, Tim ate all the chocolate in the box. Later, Tim got a big tummy ache, just like Mom warned. Tim learned to listen to Mom's warnings and never ate too much chocolate again.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a pencil on the floor. He picked it up and wanted to find the person who lost it. Tim felt helpless because he did not know who it belonged to. He tried to think of what to do.

Tim saw his friend, Sally, and asked her, "Did you lose a pencil?" Sally shook her head and said, "No, but I can help you look for the person who did." They walked around asking others if they had lost a pencil. But no one said it was theirs.

Finally, Tim and Sally saw a little girl crying. They went to her and asked, "Why are you sad?" The little girl said, "I lost my pencil and I can't draw anymore." Tim smiled and gave her the pencil. The little girl was so happy, she hugged Tim and Sally. They all became friends and played together. And from that day on, Tim learned that helping others can make you feel good, even when you feel helpless.

One day, a dog named Max went for a jog. He ran in a zigzag way, which was very fun. Max saw a big tree and thought it would be great to rest under it. While resting, he saw a little bird sitting on a branch.

"Hi, bird!" Max said. "Why do you look sad?"

"I lost my way home," the bird replied. "I don't know how to find it."

Max thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! I can jog and you can fly. We can look for your home together."

So, Max and the bird went on a great adventure. They jogged and flew, looking for the bird's home. Max jogged in a zigzag way, which made the bird laugh. The bird flew high and low, showing Max the way. Soon, they found the bird's home.

"Thank you, Max!" said the bird. "You are a good friend."

Max smiled and said, "You're welcome! Helping friends is important."

Max learned that helping others is a great thing to do. He jogged back home, feeling happy and proud.

Fluffy ran to Spot and said, "We must go back to the yard. It is safe there." Spot knew Fluffy was right. They went back to the yard and stayed there. Spot's mom was happy they listened. Spot and Fluffy played together in the yard, using their strong legs to run and jump.

The moral of the story is to listen to those who care for you and stay where it is safe. Spot and Fluffy learned that their strong legs could help them have fun, but they needed to stay in the yard to be safe.

But the little bird refused. "No, thank you. I can do it myself," said the bird. It tried and tried, but the novel was too big. The squirrel asked again, "Can I help you now?"

This time, the little bird said, "Yes, please help me." So, the squirrel and the bird worked together to carry the huge novel. They took it to the bird's nest, and they both read the story. They became good friends and shared many more books.

One day, a little girl named Lily was playing in her room. She was careful not to make a mess. She noticed that her toy bear, named Teddy, was missing. Lily looked around her room, but she could not find Teddy.

Lily walked to the window and saw the curtain moving. She pulled the curtain to the side and found Teddy hiding behind it. "There you are, Teddy!" she said. "I was looking for you."

Teddy said, "I was playing hide and seek, Lily. I'm sorry I didn't tell you." Lily smiled and gave Teddy a big hug. They played together for the rest of the day, being careful not to lose each other again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. One day, they went to the market to buy food. Lily liked to watch all the people at the market. There were many things to see and do.

At the market, Lily saw a rich man. He had a big bag of candy. Lily wanted some candy, but her mom said no. The rich man heard Lily and her mom talking. He walked over to them and said, "Would you like some candy?"

Lily's eyes grew wide and she said, "Yes, please!" But her mom said, "No, thank you. We have enough food at home." Lily was sad, but she knew her mom was right. They didn't need the candy.

As they walked away, the rich man called out, "Wait! I have an idea!" He gave Lily a small toy from his pocket. "This is for you," he said. Lily smiled and thanked the rich man. She learned that sometimes, it's better to have a toy than candy. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little boy named Tim was feeling anxious. He wanted to play with his ball outside, but it was raining. He looked out the window and saw a big puddle. Tim really wanted to kick the ball in the puddle.

Tim's mom saw him looking sad and asked, "Why are you sad, Tim?" Tim said, "I want to kick my ball outside, but it's raining." His mom thought for a moment and said, "Why don't we play inside with your soft ball? You can still kick the ball and have fun."

Tim's face lit up with a smile. He got his soft ball and started kicking it around the room. His mom joined in too, and they both laughed and played together. The rain didn't bother Tim anymore because he was having so much fun with his mom. It turned out to be a great day after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big, red ball. One day, he played with the ball in his house.

Tim threw the ball, and it hit a glass. The glass fell and broke. Tim's mom heard the noise and came in. She saw the broken glass and said, "Oh no! What happened?"

Tim felt sad and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I was playing with my ball, and it hit the glass." His mom was not fierce. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tim. We can clean it up together."

They cleaned up the broken glass and put it in the trash. Tim promised to be more careful when playing with his ball inside the house. His mom smiled and said, "That's a good boy, Tim. Let's go play outside now."

From that day on, Tim always played with his ball outside, and nothing like that ever happened again.

Bunny started to cry and ran away. Chicky felt bad for hurting her friend. She found Bunny hiding under a bush. Chicky said, "I am sorry, Bunny. Please forgive me." But Bunny was still very sad and did not want to forgive Chicky.

"Tim, soap is not good to chew. It is for washing our hands," Mom said. Tim's face turned red as he felt silly for chewing the soap.

From that day on, Tim always asked his mom before trying something new. He learned that not everything that looks good is good to eat. And they lived happily, washing their hands with soap and eating good food together.

"Be careful, Tom," Lily says. "The dog might bite you."

The man sees Tom and Lily. He smiles. He walks to them.

"Don't worry, kids," the man says. "This is Rex. He is a good dog. He won't bite you. He likes to play, too."

The man lets Tom and Lily pet Rex. Rex wags his tail. He licks Tom and Lily's faces. They giggle.

"Can we play with Rex?" Tom asks.

"Sure, you can," the man says. "But only for a little while. Rex and I have to go soon. We have to guard the bank."

"Me too," Tom says.

"Let's go home," Lily says.

"OK," Tom says.

"Bye, Rex," Tom says. "You are a nice dog."

Sara was a bossy girl. She liked to tell her friends what to do and what to play. She did not like to share her toys or listen to others. One day, she had a tea party with her dolls and stuffed animals. She put a napkin on each plate and poured some water in the cups.

"Hello, my guests," she said. "I am the queen of this party and you have to do what I say. You have to drink your water and eat your napkin. You have to say thank you and please. You have to be nice and quiet. Do you understand?"

The dolls and stuffed animals did not answer. They just looked at Sara with their button eyes and stitched mouths. Sara did not care. She was happy to be the boss.

But then, something strange happened. The napkin on her plate began to grow. It grew bigger and bigger, until it covered the whole table. It grew so big that it touched the floor and the walls. It grew so big that it wrapped around Sara and lifted her up.

"Help!" Sara cried. "What is happening? Let me go!"

The napkin did not listen. It was angry at Sara for being so bossy and rude. It wanted to teach her a lesson. It said in a loud voice, "Now you have to do what I say. You have to be nice and quiet. You have to say thank you and please. You have to drink your water and eat your napkin. Do you understand?"

Sara was scared and sorry. She did not like to be bossed around. She realized that she had been mean to her friends and her toys. She said in a small voice, "I understand. I am sorry. Please let me go."

The napkin heard Sara's words. It saw that she was sincere. It decided to give her a chance. It said in a softer voice, "Okay, I will let you go. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise to be kind and share and listen. You have to promise to be a good friend and a good queen. Do you promise?"

Sara nodded. She said, "I promise. I promise to be better. Thank you for showing me my mistake."

The napkin smiled. It said, "You're welcome. I hope you learned your lesson." It shrank back to its normal size and let Sara go. Sara hugged her dolls and stuffed animals and apologized to them. She invited them to join her tea party and have some fun. She was no longer a bossy girl. She was a happy girl.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The new dog's lack of collar foreshadows his fate of being caught by the catcher. Tom's red collar pays off when it inspires the man to give Rex a blue collar and a home.

"Tommy, Tommy, stop that racket!" a voice shouted. It was the music shop staff. He was angry and red. He came to Tommy and took the guitar away from him. "You are not allowed to play with this guitar. It is very expensive and delicate. You could break it or scratch it. You have to ask first and be respectful."

Tommy felt embarrassed and scared. He did not mean to be bad. He just wanted to have fun and learn. He looked at his mom, who was also embarrassed and sorry. She apologized to the staff and tried to calm Tommy down.

But it was too late. The staff said they had to leave the shop and never come back. He said Tommy was a naughty and rude boy who did not know how to behave. He said he would tell all the other shops to ban them too.

Tommy and his mom left the shop, feeling sad and ashamed. Tommy cried and said he was sorry. He said he still wanted to learn how to play the guitar. His mom hugged him and said she loved him, but he had to be more careful and polite next time. She said they would look for another shop or a teacher who could help him learn. But Tommy was not sure if he would ever find one. He felt like he had ruined his chance to play the guitar. He wished he had never seen it.

Tom and Lily were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and houses with the blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes.

But their baby brother Ben did not like the blocks. He liked to crawl and grab and throw things. He saw the blocks and wanted to play with them too. He crawled to the living room and disturbed Tom and Lily's game.

"Hey, stop that!" Tom shouted. He was angry because Ben knocked down his tower. "You are ruining our game!"

"No, no, no!" Lily cried. She was sad because Ben threw her bridge. "You are breaking our blocks!"

Ben did not understand. He thought they were playing with him. He laughed and clapped his hands. He saw a large block with a zero on it. He liked the zero. He grabbed the block and put it in his mouth.

"Yuck, don't do that!" Tom said. He ran to Ben and took the block from him. "That is not food, that is a block!"

"Give it back, give it back!" Ben whined. He reached for the block and pulled Tom's hair. "That is mine, that is mine!"

Tom and Lily started to cry. They did not like Ben. They wanted him to go away. They called their mom.

"Mom, mom, help!" they said. "Ben is disturbing us! He is taking our blocks and putting them in his mouth!"

Mom heard their cries and came to the living room. She saw the mess and the tears. She felt sorry for Tom and Lily and angry with Ben.

"Ben, what are you doing?" she asked. She took Ben from the floor and held him in her arms. "You are not being nice. You are disturbing your brother and sister. You have to share and play gently with the blocks. Say sorry to Tom and Lily."

Ben looked at Mom and then at Tom and Lily. He saw their sad faces. He felt a little sorry. He said in a small voice, "Sorry, sorry."

Mom smiled and kissed Ben. She said, "That's good, Ben. Now, let's clean up the blocks and play together nicely. OK?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They wiped their tears and smiled too. They said, "OK, OK."

They helped Mom to pick up the blocks and put them in a box. Then they took some blocks and gave them to Ben. They showed him how to stack them and make shapes with them. Ben liked that. He smiled and clapped his hands. He said, "Thank you, thank you."

They played together nicely with the blocks. They did not disturb each other. They had fun. Mom was happy. She said, "Good job, kids. I love you all."

Sara and Ben went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. They liked to watch them and learn their names. But their favorite animal was the seal. The seal was big and gray, and had a shiny coat. It could swim very fast and jump out of the water. It also made funny noises, like "arf arf".

The seal was curious, too. It liked to see the people who came to visit. It would swim close to the glass and look at them with its big eyes. Sometimes it would wave its flipper or clap its mouth. Sara and Ben thought the seal was very cute and smart. They wanted to play with it.

They asked their mom if they could feed the seal some fish. Their mom said yes, but they had to follow the rules. The rules were: don't touch the glass, don't throw anything in the water, and don't tease the seal. Sara and Ben said they understood and promised to be good.

They got some fish from the zookeeper and waited for their turn. When it was their turn, they held the fish in their hands and showed them to the seal. The seal was happy and came closer. It opened its mouth and took the fish gently. It thanked them with a loud "arf arf". Sara and Ben smiled and gave the seal more fish.

But then, Ben had a bad idea. He wanted to see what the seal would do if he pretended to give it a fish, but then pulled it back. He thought it would be funny. He did not listen to his mom or the rules. He held a fish in his hand and waved it in front of the seal. The seal was excited and reached for it. But Ben quickly pulled it back and laughed. He did it again and again. The seal was confused and sad. It did not like this game. It felt hurt and angry.

Sara saw what Ben was doing and did not like it either. She knew it was wrong and mean. She reminded Ben of the rules and told him to stop. She said the seal was their friend and they should be nice to it. She said if they were not nice, the seal would not like them anymore. She said they should say sorry and give the seal the fish.

Ben realized he was wrong and felt sorry. He stopped his bad game and said sorry to the seal. He gave the seal the fish and stroked its head. The seal forgave him and smiled. It arfed happily and waved its flipper. Sara and Ben hugged the seal and said goodbye. They learned their lesson and never teased the seal again.

The moral of the story is: don't tease or hurt animals, they have feelings too. Be kind and respectful to them, and they will be your friends.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the woods behind their house. They liked to look for bugs, birds and flowers. They also liked to listen to the creek that ran through the woods. The creek made a nice sound, like a song.

One day, Ben and Lily decided to follow the creek and see where it went. They walked and walked, holding hands. They saw many new things, like a big rock, a fallen tree and a frog. They were having fun.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was a growl, like a big dog. Ben and Lily stopped and looked around. They saw a big bear, standing on the other side of the creek. The bear looked angry and hungry. It saw Ben and Lily and started to move towards them.

Ben and Lily were scared. They wanted to run away, but they did not know which way to go. They did not want to cross the creek, because the water was deep and cold. They did not want to go back, because the bear might follow them. They did not know what to do.

Then, Lily remembered what her mom had told her. She said, "Ben, we have to ignore the bear. We have to be very still and quiet. We have to pretend we are not here. Maybe the bear will go away."

Ben nodded. He trusted his sister. They both sat down on the ground and hugged each other. They closed their eyes and tried to ignore the bear. They tried to ignore the growl, the steps and the sniffs. They tried to ignore their fear.

They did not know how long they sat there. They felt restless and cold. They wanted to go home. They wanted their mom and dad. But they did not move or make a sound.

After a while, they heard the bear leave. They opened their eyes and saw that the bear was gone. They saw the creek, shining in the sun. They saw the woods, green and calm. They felt relieved and happy.

They got up and ran back to their house. They told their mom and dad what had happened. They hugged them and thanked them. They said they were brave and smart. They said they were proud of them.

Ben and Lily learned a lesson that day. They learned to ignore the bear. They learned to listen to the creek. They learned to love each other.

"Ben, no! Stop!" Mom said. But it was too late. Ben took a big bite of his food and started to cough and cry.

"Water! Water!" Ben shouted. He grabbed his glass and drank it all. Then he knocked over the sauce bottle and it spilled on the table. The sauce scattered all over the place and stained the tablecloth.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Lily. I was curious and I wanted to try something new. But I learned my lesson. Spicy sauce is not for me. And I should not touch things that are not mine," Ben said.

Lily was a poor girl who lived with her mother in a small hut. They did not have much to eat or wear, but they loved each other very much. Every day, Lily would go out and gather sticks and stones to make a fire and a fence. She also liked to look for shiny things that she could keep in her pocket.

One day, as she was gathering sticks, she saw something white and hard on the ground. She picked it up and saw that it was a tooth. She wondered who had lost it and why. She thought it was very pretty and shiny, so she put it in her pocket and ran back to her mother.

"Look, mama, what I found!" she said, showing her the tooth. "It is so white and hard and shiny!"

Her mother smiled and hugged her. "That is a very nice tooth, my dear. Do you know what kind of tooth it is?"

Lily shook her head. She did not know much about teeth.

"It is a lion's tooth, my dear. A very brave and strong animal. It must have fallen out when he was hunting or fighting. You are very lucky to find it. It is a sign of courage and power."

Lily's eyes widened. She felt very proud and happy. She had a lion's tooth in her pocket!

"Can I keep it, mama? Can I wear it around my neck?"

"Of course, my dear. You can keep it and wear it as a necklace. It will protect you and make you strong. But you must also be kind and gentle, like a lioness with her cubs. That is the true mark of a lion's heart."

Lily nodded and hugged her mother. She thanked her and kissed her. She felt very rich and blessed. She had a lion's tooth and a mother's love.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to learn new things. One day, their dad brought home a big box from his work. He said it was a surprise for them. He opened the box and took out a shiny tool with a round glass on top. He said it was a microscope.

"What is a microscope, dad?" Ben asked.

"A microscope is a tool that helps you see very small things that you cannot see with your eyes. Like bugs, or flowers, or hair," dad explained.

"Wow, can we try it?" Lily asked.

"Sure, let me show you how it works. You need to put something on this slide and then look through the glass. Be careful not to touch the glass with your fingers," dad said.

He took a leaf from a plant and cut a small piece. He put it on the slide and turned on a light under it. He invited Ben and Lily to take turns looking through the microscope.

Ben went first. He put his eye close to the glass and gasped. He saw many tiny green dots and lines on the leaf. He said, "It looks like a map, dad. What are those dots and lines?"

"Those are cells, Ben. They are the building blocks of living things. They have different shapes and colors depending on what they do," dad said.

Lily went next. She put her eye close to the glass and smiled. She saw many tiny red and blue dots and lines on the leaf. She said, "It looks like a painting, dad. What are those dots and lines?"

"Those are veins, Lily. They carry water and food to the cells. They have different colors depending on the direction of the flow," dad said.

Ben and Lily were amazed by what they saw. They thanked their dad for the surprise and asked him to show them more things under the microscope. They were very cheerful and curious. They learned a lot of new things that day. They loved their microscope.

One day, Jill wanted to play with water in the bathroom. She put a stool next to the sink and climbed on it. She turned on the faucet and watched the water come out. She put her hands under the water and felt how cold it was. She put a cup under the faucet and filled it with water. She poured the water on the toothbrush and on the soap and on the mirror.

She wanted to make the water warmer. She turned the faucet to the left, but it was hard to move. She turned it harder and harder, but it did not move. She got angry and pulled the faucet with all her strength. She heard a loud snap and saw the faucet come off the sink. She saw water spray everywhere, on the walls, on the ceiling, on the floor, on her.

She screamed and dropped the faucet. Tom heard her scream and ran to the bathroom. He saw the water and the faucet and Jill. He turned off the water from the other faucet and grabbed a towel. He wrapped the towel around Jill and hugged her. He said, "It's okay, Jill. It was an accident. Don't cry."

Jill cried and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I broke the faucet. I wanted to play with water."

Tom said, "I know, Jill. You like water. But you have to be careful with the faucet. It can break if you turn it too hard. Next time, ask me or Mom or Dad to help you."

Jill nodded and said, "Okay, Tom. Thank you for helping me."

Tom said, "You're welcome, Jill. I love you."

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw some snow on the ground. They put on their coats, hats, and gloves and ran outside.

"Look, Ben, snow!" Lily said. "Let's make a snowman!"

"OK, Lily, that sounds fun!" Ben said. They rolled some big balls of snow and stacked them on top of each other. They found some rocks, sticks, and a carrot to make the snowman's face and arms.

"Wow, he looks great!" Lily said. "But he looks cold. Maybe we should give him something to keep him warm."

"Like what?" Ben asked.

Lily thought for a moment. Then she ran inside the house and came back with a scarf. She wrapped it around the snowman's neck.

"Here you go, Mr. Snowman. This is my scarf. I value it very much, but you can have it. It will make you cozy and happy," she said.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very kind," the snowman said.

Lily and Ben gasped. They did not know the snowman could talk.

"Hello, Lily and Ben. I'm Frosty, the snowman. You made me very well. I like your scarf, Lily. It is very pretty and warm. You value it, and I value you," the snowman said.

Lily and Ben smiled. They were happy to have a new friend.

"Can we play with you, Frosty?" they asked.

"Of course, you can. But we have to be quick. The sun is coming out, and it will make me melt. Let's have some fun before I go," the snowman said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They played with Frosty in the snow. They threw snowballs, made snow angels, and slid on the icy hill. They had a lot of fun.

But soon, the snowman started to shrink. He became smaller and smaller.

"Oh, no, Frosty. You are melting!" Lily said.

"Don't be sad, Lily. It's OK. I had a wonderful time with you and Ben. You are the best friends a snowman could have. Thank you for your scarf. It made me feel loved. I will always remember you," the snowman said.

"We will always remember you, too, Frosty. You are the best snowman ever. We love you," Lily and Ben said.

They hugged the snowman goodbye. Then they watched him melt away.

They felt sad, but they also felt happy. They had made a special friend, and they had learned to value what they had. They went inside the house and drank some hot chocolate. They looked out the window and saw a rainbow in the sky. They smiled and thought of Frosty. They hoped he would come back someday.

The bad ending is that Lily's parents were very worried and took her to the hospital. The doctors said she had broken her leg and needed to stay in bed for a long time. Lily couldn't skip for a while, but she learned to be more careful when she went on adventures.

Tommy said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I broke your toy. I will measure it and try to fix it." Lily said, "That's okay, Tommy. You can keep the toy as a gift. I'm happy to share with my friends." 

Tommy was surprised and grateful. He thanked Lily for being so kind and gifted. From that day on, they played together with Lily's other toys and had lots of fun.

Lily and Tom were playing pirates in the garden. They had a big box, a hat, a sword and a map. The map showed them where to find the treasure. It was a very old and fragile map, so they had to be careful not to tear it.

"Let's go, matey!" Tom said, holding the map. "The treasure is this way!"

He led Lily to a corner of the garden, where there was a big tree. He looked at the map and said, "We have to turn left here and dig under the tree."

Lily followed him, but she was not sure. She looked at the map and said, "Are you sure, Tom? The map looks different from the garden. Maybe we have to turn right, not left."

Tom did not listen to her. He said, "No, no, Lily, you are wrong. I know how to read maps. Trust me, the treasure is here."

He started to dig with his sword, but he dug too hard. He hit a big rock and the sword broke. He also ripped the map by accident. He was very sad and angry.

Lily felt sorry for him. She said, "Don't worry, Tom, it's just a game. We can still have fun. Maybe we can make a new map and a new sword. Or we can play something else."

Tom looked at her and realized she was right. He said, "You are a good friend, Lily. I'm sorry I did not listen to you. You were right, the map did not match the garden. Maybe we have to turn right, not left. Or maybe the treasure is somewhere else. Let's go and find out."

They hugged and went to look for a new adventure.

The moral value of the story is to listen to others and be humble. The narrative uses foreshadowing or setup and payoff by showing that the map is old and fragile, and that it does not match the garden, which leads to Tom's mistake and the map's destruction.

A nice lady saw Anna and her mom. She had a big dog with her. The dog was brown and fluffy and had a purple collar. The lady said to Anna, "Do you like my dog? His name is Max. He likes purple too. Do you want to pet him?"

Anna stopped crying. She liked dogs. She liked purple. She looked at Max. He looked friendly and cute. She nodded to the lady. She said, "Yes, please. Can I pet him?"

The lady smiled. She said, "Of course you can. But you have to be gentle and patient. He is a good dog, but he does not like loud noises or sudden moves. Can you do that?"

Anna nodded again. She said, "Yes, I can. I can be gentle and patient. I am sorry I was loud and angry. I was just very sad. I love my purple ball."

Anna and her mom said goodbye to the lady and Max. They walked home, holding hands. They were happy and warm. They learned a lesson. They were gentle and patient. And they loved purple.
