Love and kindness are more important than money and things. I have been selfish and greedy. I have a big house and a lot of things, but I don't have many friends or happiness. Can you forgive me?"

Anna's mom smiled and said, "Of course. Everyone makes mistakes. You can learn from them and change. You can be more generous and friendly. You can share your money and things with others who need them. You can find joy in simple things. Then you will be truly wealthy."

The wealthy lady smiled too. She thanked Anna's mom and gave her a hug. She also gave Anna a gift, a new mop with colorful stripes. She said, "This is for you, Anna. You are a good girl who likes to help your mom. You have taught me a lesson today. I hope you like this mop. It is not better than your old mop, but it is more fun."

Anna was happy and said, "Thank you, lady. I like this mop. It is very pretty. I will use it to clean the house with my mom. I hope you come back and visit us again. You are our friend now."

The wealthy lady nodded and said, "I will. You are my friends too. Goodbye, Anna. Goodbye, mom."

She left the house, feeling happier than before. She decided to be more kind and generous from then on. She learned that being wealthy is not about having money and things, but about having love and kindness.

"Sure, but be careful. It is not ours. Someone might come back for it," Mom said.

Lily took the umbrella and ran to the grass. She opened and closed it. She pretended it was a tent. She pretended it was a boat. She pretended it was a flower. She had a lot of fun.

But then, the sky turned dark. The wind blew hard. The rain came down. Lily got wet and cold. She ran back to the bench. But Mom was not there.

"Mom! Mom! Where are you?" Lily cried.

She looked around. She saw Mom walking away. Mom had a big bag and a coat. Mom did not see Lily. Mom did not hear Lily. Mom forgot Lily.

Lily was scared and sad. She hugged the umbrella. She hoped Mom would come back. But Mom did not come back. Lily was alone in the park. The rain did not stop. The umbrella did not help. Lily wished she had not played with the umbrella. She wished she had stayed with Mom. She wished Mom had not forgotten her.

Anna and Ben were going to camp with their mom and dad. They were very happy. They packed their bags, their toys and their snacks. They got in the car and drove for a long time.

"Are we there yet?" Anna asked.

"Soon, sweetie," mom said. "Look, the sky is clear and blue. We can see the stars at night."

Anna looked out the window and saw the trees and the hills. She smiled. She liked the stars.

Ben was bored. He did not like the car. He wanted to play. He sighed.

"Can we play a game?" he asked.

"Sure, what game do you want to play?" dad said.

"I spy with my little eye, something that is green," Ben said.

"Is it a tree?" Anna guessed.

"No," Ben said.

"Is it a grass?" mom guessed.

"No," Ben said.

"Is it a frog?" dad guessed.

"No," Ben said. "You are all wrong. It is my shirt!"

Ben laughed. Anna, mom and dad laughed too. They had fun playing the game.

They arrived at the camp. They got out of the car and saw a big tent, a fire and a lake. They were very excited. They helped mom and dad set up the tent and the sleeping bags. They ate hot dogs and marshmallows. They sang songs and told stories. They saw the stars and the moon.

Anna and Ben hugged mom and dad. They said good night. They went to sleep in the tent. They dreamed of the camp. They were very happy.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They had a lot of fun.

But then, their mom called them. "Tom, Lily, it's time to go home. The sun is going down and it will be dark soon."

Tom and Lily did not want to go home. They wanted to keep playing. They said, "No, mom, please, just a little more. We want to see the sunset. It is so pretty and colorful."

Their mom was grumpy. She said, "No, you have to go home now. You have to eat dinner and take a bath and go to bed. You can see the sunset tomorrow. Come on, let's go."

Tom and Lily were sad. They picked up their ball and followed their mom. They looked at the sky and saw the sun getting lower and lower. They missed the sunset. They wished they could stay in the park. They hoped they could see the sunset tomorrow.

Lily was a big girl who liked to do things by herself. She was independent and did not need help from anyone. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a big bench. She wanted to sit on it and pretend it was a boat.

"Mom, can I sit on the bench?" she asked.

"Sure, honey, but be careful. The bench is heavy and you might fall off," her mom said.

Lily nodded and ran to the bench. She climbed on it and sat in the middle. She felt proud and happy. She waved to her mom and said, "Look, mom, I'm on a boat!"

Her mom smiled and watched her. She was glad that Lily was having fun and learning new things.

But then, Lily had an idea. She wanted to see how much the bench weighed. She got up and tried to lift one end of the bench. She pushed and pulled, but the bench did not move. It was too heavy for her.

"Mom, how much does the bench weigh?" she asked.

"I don't know, honey, but it's a lot. You can't lift it by yourself. You need help from someone stronger," her mom said.

Lily frowned. She did not like to need help. She wanted to be independent and do everything by herself. She tried to lift the bench again, but it still did not move. She felt frustrated and angry.

"Mom, I don't need help. I can do it by myself. I'm a big girl!" she said.

Her mom sighed and walked to her. She hugged her and said, "I know, honey, you're a big girl and you can do many things by yourself. But sometimes, it's okay to need help. It doesn't mean you're not independent. It means you're smart and brave. You can ask for help when you need it, and you can help others when they need it. That's what makes you a good friend and a good person."

Lily thought about what her mom said. She realized that her mom was right. She smiled and said, "Okay, mom, I understand. Thank you for helping me. Can we sit on the bench together and pretend it's a boat?"

"Of course, honey, I would love that," her mom said.

They sat on the bench and hugged each other. They pretended it was a boat and sailed to different places. They had a lot of fun and learned a lot. They were independent and happy.

Lily did not like vegetables. She thought they were boring and yucky. She only wanted to eat cake and candy and ice cream. Every day, she would demand that her mom give her sweets for dinner. But her mom knew that vegetables were good for Lily. They made her strong and healthy and smart.

One day, mom had a surprise for Lily. She made a vegetable cake. It looked like a chocolate cake, but it had carrots and zucchini and spinach inside. She put some frosting and sprinkles on top to make it pretty. She told Lily that it was a special cake for her.

Lily was very happy. She loved cake. She took a big bite and waited for the sweet taste. But instead, she tasted something bitter and green. She spit it out and made a face. She said, "This is not cake! This is vegetable! I hate vegetable!"

Mom smiled and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I wanted to show you that vegetables can be fun and tasty. They are not boring. They have different colors and shapes and flavors. You can make many things with them. You can make soup and salad and pizza and even cake. But you have to try them first. Will you try another bite?"

Lily looked at the cake. She saw the frosting and the sprinkles. She saw the carrots and the zucchini and the spinach. She was curious. She wondered what they would taste like together. She decided to try another bite. She took a small bite and chewed slowly. She was surprised. It was not bad. It was sweet and moist and crunchy. She said, "This is not bad. This is good. I like vegetable cake!"

Mom was very happy. She hugged Lily and said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily. You are a brave and smart girl. You tried something new and learned something new. You can have more cake if you want. But you also have to eat other vegetables. They are good for you. They are your friends. Will you eat other vegetables?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I will eat other vegetables. But can I have some ice cream too?"

Mom laughed and said, "Yes, Lily. You can have some ice cream too. But only a little. And only after you finish your vegetables."

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. But sometimes they do not behave. They fight over who gets what. They make a lot of noise. They do not listen to Mom and Dad.

One day, Mom and Dad have to go out. They ask Grandma to watch Sara and Tom. Grandma is very nice. She makes them cookies and milk. She reads them stories. She gives them hugs and kisses.

But Sara and Tom still do not behave. They want more cookies and milk. They do not share their toys and books. They do not say please and thank you. They make a mess in the living room.

Grandma is not happy. She tells Sara and Tom to stop. She says they have to behave. She says they have to be kind and polite. She says they have to clean up their mess.

Sara and Tom do not listen. They keep fighting and yelling. They throw their toys and books. They spill their milk. They break a teaspoon.

Grandma is very sad. She says she is disappointed in Sara and Tom. She says they have to go to their room. She says they have to stay there until Mom and Dad come back.

Sara and Tom feel bad. They see Grandma's sad face. They see the broken teaspoon. They see the mess they made. They realize they were wrong. They say they are sorry to Grandma. They say they love her.

Grandma smiles. She says she loves them too. She says she forgives them. She says they can come out of their room. She says they can help her clean up.

Sara and Tom are glad. They hug Grandma. They help her clean up. They say please and thank you. They share their toys and books. They behave.

Mom and Dad come back. They see the clean living room. They see the happy faces. They praise Sara and Tom. They thank Grandma. They hug and kiss everyone.

Sara and Tom are very glad. They learned a lesson. They say they will behave from now on. They say they love Mom, Dad, and Grandma. They say they had a good day.

Tom and Lily are thirsty. They want to drink something cool and sweet. They see some oranges on the table. They ask Mom if they can have some.

"Can we have some orange juice, Mom?" Tom says.

"Sure, you can, but you have to make it yourself," Mom says. "Do you know how to squeeze the oranges?"

Tom and Lily nod. They have seen Mom do it before. They take two oranges and a big bowl. They cut the oranges in half with a knife. They are careful not to cut themselves.

They take one orange half each and squeeze it hard over the bowl. They feel the juice come out of the orange and drip into the bowl. They squeeze and squeeze until there is no more juice in the orange. They do the same with the other halves.

They look at the bowl. It is full of orange juice. It looks yummy. They pour the juice into two cups. They drink it. It is cool and sweet. It makes them happy.

"Yum, this is the best juice ever!" Lily says.

"I agree, we made it ourselves!" Tom says.

They smile at each other. They thank Mom for the oranges. They are proud of their juice. They want to squeeze more oranges later.

One day, a hungry beetle was looking for food. He saw a big apple on a tree. He wanted to eat it, but it was too high for him. He tried to climb the tree, but he fell down. He tried to fly, but he was too heavy. He tried to ask other bugs for help, but they were busy or scared.

He felt sad and tired. He was about to give up, when he saw a worm. The worm was also hungry, and he was also looking for food. He saw the apple, too, but he knew he could not reach it. He had an idea. He said to the beetle, "Hello, friend. I have a plan. If we work together, we can get the apple. Do you want to try?"

The beetle was curious. He said, "Yes, I do. What is your plan?" The worm said, "You can carry me on your back, and I can dig a hole in the apple. Then we can both eat it. What do you think?" The beetle liked the plan. He said, "That sounds good. Let's do it."

So they did. The beetle lifted the worm on his back, and flew to the apple. The worm dug a hole in the apple, and made a tunnel for them. They both ate the apple, and shared it. They were happy and full. They thanked each other, and became friends.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes, we can solve our problems by working together and helping each other.

Anna and Ben liked to play in the living room. They had many toys and books and games. But their favorite thing was the fireplace. It was big and warm and made funny sounds. Sometimes they saw sparks and smoke and shapes in the fire.

One day, Anna and Ben decided to play a game. They wanted to see who could disappear behind the fireplace. They took turns hiding and counting and finding each other. They had a lot of fun and laughed a lot.

But then, something strange happened. Anna hid behind the fireplace and Ben counted to ten. He said, "Ready or not, here I come!" He looked behind the fireplace, but he did not see Anna. He looked again, but she was not there. He called her name, but she did not answer. He started to feel scared. Where did Anna go?

He ran to the kitchen and told his mom. His mom was surprised and worried. She followed him to the living room and looked behind the fireplace. She saw a small door that Ben and Anna had never noticed before. She opened the door and saw a dark tunnel. She called Anna's name, but there was no reply. She took Ben's hand and said, "Let's go find your sister."

They walked into the tunnel and saw a light at the end. They came out into a beautiful garden. There were flowers and trees and birds and butterflies. And there was Anna. She was sitting on a swing and smiling. She saw Ben and mom and said, "Hi! I found a secret place. It's so pretty and quiet. Do you want to play with me?"

Ben and mom were happy and relieved. They hugged Anna and said, "We were so worried about you. How did you get here?"

Anna pointed to the fireplace and said, "I just followed the fire. It showed me the way. It was like magic."

Ben and mom looked at the fireplace and saw that it was still burning. But it was not noisy anymore. It was soft and gentle and friendly. They smiled and said, "That's amazing. Maybe the fire likes you. Maybe it wanted to share its secret with you."

They decided to stay in the garden for a while and play with Anna. They had a wonderful time. They thanked the fire for its gift and promised to come back soon. They went back to the living room and closed the door behind the fireplace. They never told anyone about their adventure. It was their special secret.

Sam and Mia liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. They made roads and bridges with blocks and books. They zoomed their cars along the roads and made noises like vroom and beep.

One day, they found a pebble in the garden. It was shiny and smooth and had spots of red and blue. Sam said, "Look, Mia, a new car!" He put the pebble on a block and pretended it was a car. He zoomed it along the road and said, "This is the fastest car ever!"

Mia said, "No, Sam, that is not a car. That is a pebble. It is a rock. It cannot zoom. It cannot beep. It is not a car." She took the pebble from Sam and threw it away.

Sam was sad. He liked the pebble. He thought it was a special car. He ran after the pebble and picked it up. He said, "Mia, you are wrong. This is a car. It is a magic car. It can zoom and beep and fly. It is not a normal car. It is a better car."

Mia said, "Sam, you are silly. That is not a magic car. That is a pebble. It is a rock. It cannot fly. It is not a better car. It is a worse car." She took the pebble from Sam and threw it away again.

Sam was angry. He did not like Mia. He thought she was mean. He ran after the pebble and picked it up. He said, "Mia, you are mean. This is my car. It is a magic car. It is a better car. I do not want to play with you. I want to play with my car." He zoomed away with the pebble and left Mia alone.

Lily and Max were playing with their toy guns in the garden. They liked to pretend they were cowboys and Indians. Lily wore a hat and a belt with a gun. Max wore a feather on his head and a bow and arrow.

"Bang, bang, you're dead!" Lily shouted, pointing her gun at Max.

"No, I'm not! You missed me!" Max said, dodging behind a bush.

He pulled his bow and shot an arrow at Lily. The arrow had a soft tip, so it did not hurt. But it hit Lily's hat and knocked it off.

"Hey, that's not fair! You shot my hat!" Lily cried, picking up her hat.

"It is fair! You shot at me first!" Max said, sticking out his tongue.

They glared at each other, ready to shoot again. But then they heard a loud noise. It was their dog, Spot. Spot was a big, chubby dog who liked to chase things. He saw the feather on Max's head and thought it was a bird. He ran towards Max, barking and wagging his tail.

"Spot, no! Leave me alone!" Max yelled, dropping his bow and arrow.

He tried to run away, but Spot was faster. He jumped on Max and licked his face. He also grabbed the feather and pulled it off.

"Spot, bad dog! Give me back my feather!" Max said, trying to get the feather.

But Spot thought it was a game. He ran away with the feather in his mouth.

Lily saw what happened and laughed. She forgot about being angry with Max. She ran after Spot, too.

"Come on, Max, let's catch Spot and get your feather back!" she said.

"OK, Lily, let's go!" Max said.

They chased Spot around the garden, having fun. They did not shoot at each other anymore. They were friends again.

"Look, Tom! What is that?" Lily asks.

"I don't know, Lily. It is very pretty. Maybe it is a ball," Tom says.

They run to the big round thing. They want to touch it. But it is too high. They cannot reach it.

They look around. They see a man. He has a hat and a coat. He smiles at them.

"Who are you?" Lily asks.

"I am Mr. Sun. I am the big round thing. I make the day warm and bright," the man says.

"Wow! You are Mr. Sun? Can we talk to you?" Tom asks.

"Of course. I like to talk to children. You are very curious and kind," the man says.

Lily and Tom are happy. They talk to Mr. Sun. They ask him many questions. He tells them many stories. They have fun. They learn a lot. They thank Mr. Sun for talking to them.

"Goodbye, children. I have to go now. But I will come back tomorrow. And you can talk to me again," Mr. Sun says.

"Goodbye, Mr. Sun. Thank you for being our friend," Lily and Tom say.

They wave to Mr. Sun. He waves back. He goes behind the trees. He makes the sky orange and pink. Lily and Tom go home. They tell their parents about Mr. Sun. They are very happy. They can't wait to see him again.

"Ha ha, this boat is mine now!" the witch cackled. She reached out her hand to grab it. But the toy boat was red, and red was the color that the witch hated the most. It made her feel sick and angry.

Lily was an adventurous girl who liked to explore new things. One day, she saw a vendor with a big cart full of colorful balloons. She wanted to buy one, but she had no money.

"Can I have a balloon, please?" she asked the vendor.

"Sure, but you have to pay me one number for each balloon. How many numbers do you have?" the vendor said.

Lily did not know what a number was. She thought it was something shiny and pretty, like a star. She looked around and saw a necklace on a lady's neck. It had many numbers on it.

"I have many numbers!" she said, and ran to the lady. She tried to grab the necklace, but the lady screamed and pushed her away.

"Help! Thief! Thief!" the lady shouted.

Lily was scared and confused. She did not understand why the lady was angry. She just wanted a balloon. She ran back to the vendor, but he was gone. He had taken his cart and left.

Lily was alone and sad. She had no balloon, no number, and no friend. She had done a bad thing, and now she was in trouble.

The moral of the story is: Do not take things that do not belong to you. Ask before you touch. Learn what words mean before you use them.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They had a big box of toys and a shovel. They liked to dig holes and bury their toys. Then they would pretend to be pirates and look for treasure.

"Look, I found a magic wand!" Lily said, holding a shiny stick. "I can make anything happen with this!"

"Really? Can you make me a cake?" Tom asked, licking his lips.

"OK, let me try. Abracadabra, cake for Tom!" Lily waved the wand and pointed at Tom.

But nothing happened. Tom was still hungry and sad.

"Maybe you need to say something else," he said.

"OK, how about this? Hocus pocus, cake for Tom!" Lily tried again.

But still nothing happened. Tom was still hungry and sad.

"Maybe the wand is broken," he said.

"Bald? Why bald?" Tom asked, confused.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they found a bottle of wine in the kitchen. They thought it was juice and wanted to drink it.

"Let's pretend we are grown-ups and have a party," Tom said.

"OK, but we have to be careful. Mom and Dad said we can't touch the wine," Lily said.

They poured some wine into two cups and went to the living room. They put on some fake hats and glasses and pretended to talk like grown-ups.

"Hello, sir. How are you today?" Tom asked.

"Very well, thank you. And you, madam?" Lily answered.

"I'm fine, thank you. This is a lovely party. Would you like some more wine?" Tom offered.

"Yes, please. This wine is very tasty. It makes me feel funny," Lily said.

They drank more and more wine until they felt dizzy and sick. They started to giggle and stumble and spill the wine on the carpet.

Suddenly, they heard the door open. It was Mom and Dad. They saw the mess and the wine and the twins.

"What are you doing?" Mom asked.

"We are playing pretend," Tom said.

"We are grown-ups," Lily said.

Mom and Dad were very angry and sad. They took the wine and the cups and the fake hats and glasses. They made the twins sit on the couch and explained to them why they should never drink wine.

"Wine is not juice. It is not for kids. It is for grown-ups who drink it carefully. It can make you sick and hurt your body and your brain. It can also make you do bad things and get in trouble. You should never touch the wine or any other drink like that. Do you understand?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom. We are sorry. We didn't know. We won't do it again," Tom and Lily said.

Mom and Dad hugged them and said they loved them. They also said they had to clean the carpet and go to bed early. They said they hoped they learned their lesson.

The twins nodded and said they did. They realized that playing pretend was fun, but not with wine. They also learned that being grown-up was not easy and that they should listen to their parents. They decided to rise early the next day and say sorry again and help with the chores. They also decided to play with their toys and books instead of the wine. They knew that was the right thing to do.

But she reached too far. She lost her balance. She fell to the floor. She hit her head. She felt dizzy. She started to cry.

Her mom heard her cry. She ran to the living room. She saw Jenny on the floor. She saw the real telephone and the toy telephone. She understood what happened. She picked up Jenny and hugged her. She said, "Oh, Jenny. I'm sorry. Are you okay? Did you hurt yourself?"

Jenny sobbed. She said, "Mom, I'm dizzy. I wanted to see the real telephone. I wanted to talk to uncle Tom. But I fell. And I dropped the telephone. And I lost uncle Tom."

Her mom said, "Don't worry, Jenny. You didn't lose uncle Tom. He's still on the line. He's waiting for you. Here, take the telephone. Say hello to him. He loves you very much. And so do I."

Jenny took the telephone. She heard her uncle Tom's voice. He said, "Hello, Jenny. Are you okay? I heard you fall. I was worried about you."

Jenny said, "Hi, uncle Tom. I'm okay. I'm sorry I dropped the telephone. I love you too. And I love mom. And I love my toy telephone. Thank you for calling. You made me happy."

It is pretty and rare!" The lady says, "I see. But you know, there are many minerals in the world. And they are not more important than your friendship. Why don't you share the rock and play together?"

Lila and Ben think about what the lady says. They feel sorry for being mean to each other. They say, "You are right, lady. Thank you for being kind. We will share the rock and play together." The lady smiles and says, "You are welcome, children. I am glad you are friends again. Have fun!"

Lila and Ben decide to play a game with the rock. They take turns to spin it on the ground and see what color it shows. They laugh and have fun. They are happy and forget about their fight. They learn that sharing is better than fighting. And they thank the lady and her dog for being compassionate.

Tom and Mia were friends who liked to play in the garden. They had a small patch of dirt where they planted seeds and watered them every day. They were very happy when they saw green leaves and flowers grow from the seeds.

One day, they saw a red pepper hanging from a plant. They both wanted to pick it and eat it. They ran towards the pepper and pulled at it with their hands.

"Let go, it's mine!" Tom shouted.

"No, it's mine!" Mia shouted back.

They pulled harder and harder, but the pepper did not yield. It was very strong and firm. They did not notice that they were pulling the plant out of the ground too.

Suddenly, they heard a loud snap and felt a sting on their fingers. The pepper had broken off the plant and sprayed juice in their eyes. They dropped the pepper and screamed in pain. They rubbed their eyes and cried.

The pepper rolled away and landed in front of a big dog. The dog sniffed the pepper and licked it. He liked the spicy taste and ate the pepper in one bite. He wagged his tail and barked happily.

Tom and Mia heard the bark and opened their eyes. They saw the dog with the pepper in his mouth. They felt very sad and angry. They had lost their pepper and hurt their eyes. They blamed each other for being clumsy and greedy. They stopped being friends and went home. They never played in the garden again.

"Look how high it goes!" Tim said, as he tossed the ball to Kim.

"I can catch it!" Kim said, as she jumped to reach the ball.

But the ball was too high for Kim. It flew over her head and hit a vase on the shelf. The vase was very old and pretty. It had flowers and birds on it. It belonged to their grandma, who loved it very much. The vase fell to the floor and broke into many pieces.

"Oh no!" Tim and Kim said, as they saw the mess.

They heard their grandma coming from the kitchen. She was bald, because she had no hair. She wore a scarf on her head. She was very kind and sweet, but she did not like when things broke.

"What was that noise?" she asked, as she entered the living room.

She saw the broken vase and the ball. She saw Tim and Kim, who looked scared and sad.

"Grandma, we are sorry!" they said. "We did not mean to break your vase. We were playing with the ball and it hit the vase. We like your vase. It is very pretty."

Grandma looked at them and sighed. She was not happy, but she was not angry either. She loved her grandchildren more than anything.

"I know you did not mean to break it," she said. "But you have to be careful when you play. The vase was very old and special. It was a gift from my mom, who is in heaven. She gave it to me when I was a little girl, like you."

She picked up the pieces of the vase and put them in a box. She hugged Tim and Kim and kissed them.

"I forgive you," she said. "But you have to promise me something. Next time, play with the ball outside, or in your room. And be more gentle with your toys. They can excite you, but they can also hurt you or other things."

Tim and Kim nodded and said sorry again. They promised to be more careful. They gave Grandma their ball and asked her to play with them. Grandma smiled and agreed. She took the ball and threw it to Tim. They played catch and laughed. They forgot about the vase and had fun.

They hear a noise behind them. It is the bull. He sees them and runs towards them. He wants to get them. Tom and Sue are very scared. They drop the box and run away. They hide behind a fence and hope the bull will not find them.

He roars and tries to break free, but he cannot.

Tom and Sue see what happens. They are happy. They are not scared anymore. They laugh and clap their hands. They say to each other:

"Good job, Tom and Sue! You helped me catch the bull!"

He takes the bull out of the hole and puts him in a cage. He says he will sell the bull to another farm. He says the bull will not bother them anymore.

Tommy loved to imagine. He liked to pretend he was a knight, a pirate, a superhero, or anything else he could think of. He had a big box of toys and costumes that he used to make his stories come to life. Sometimes he played with his friends, and sometimes he played by himself.

One day, Tommy decided to imagine he was a farmer. He put on a straw hat and a plaid shirt, and he took a wooden spoon and a bowl. He went outside to his backyard, where he had a small patch of dirt. He pretended the dirt was his farm, and he planted some oats. He used the spoon to dig holes and drop the oats in. He watered them with a hose, and he sang a song about how he would make oatmeal and cookies and bread with his oats.

He was so busy imagining, he didn't notice the dark clouds in the sky. He didn't hear the thunder or see the lightning. He didn't feel the raindrops until they were big and heavy and wet. He looked up and saw the storm. He was scared. He ran inside, leaving his hat, his shirt, his spoon, and his bowl behind.

Her mom heard her cry and came to help her. She picked her up and hugged her. She said, "Lily, I told you it was too hot to play outside. You are dehydrated and sunburned. Can you forgive me?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, I forgive you. I love you, Lily. You are my sweet girl. But next time, please do what I say. It is for your own good." Lily nodded again and said, "I love you too, mom. And I will do what you say next time. Thank you for the water and ice cream." They went inside and Lily felt better.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your mom when she tells you something. She knows what is best for you and she wants you to be healthy and happy.

"Please, let us do the spell," said Mia. "We are sorry. We don't want you to be alive. We want you to be our toys again."

The toys did not want to listen. They tried to stop Ben and Mia. But Ben and Mia were brave and smart. They worked together and said the words and blew out the candles. The toys stopped moving and talking. They were toys again.

Ben and Mia hugged each other and their toys. They were glad that everything was back to normal. They learned a lesson. Tom was a little boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a lot of cars, trains, and planes that he zoomed around the floor. He also had a cat named Fluffy, who was his best friend. Fluffy liked to nap on Tom's bed, chase mice, and drink milk.

One day, Tom's mom told him to come to the kitchen for lunch. She had made him a sandwich and some juice. Tom was hungry, but he wanted to play a little more. He said, "Mom, can I play for five more minutes?" Mom said, "No, Tom, you need to eat now. Your food will get cold and your juice will get warm. Come now, or you will have no lunch."

Tom did not listen to his mom. He said, "OK, OK, I will come soon." But he did not come soon. He played and played, and forgot about his lunch. He also forgot about Fluffy, who was thirsty. Fluffy saw Tom's juice on the table, and thought it was milk. He jumped on the table, and licked the juice. But the juice was not milk. It was grape juice, and it was bad for cats. Fluffy felt sick, and fell off the table. He did not move.

Tom heard a thud, and looked at the table. He saw Fluffy on the floor, and ran to him. He said, "Fluffy, Fluffy, are you OK?" But Fluffy did not answer. He did not purr, or meow, or blink. He was dead. Tom cried, and cried, and cried. He said, "I'm sorry, Fluffy, I'm sorry. I should have come to lunch. I should have given you milk. I love you, Fluffy, I love you."

Mom heard Tom's cries, and came to the living room. She saw Fluffy on the floor, and Tom on his knees. She hugged Tom, and said, "I'm sorry, Tom, I'm sorry. Fluffy is gone. He drank something bad, and it hurt him. He was a good cat, and he loved you too."

Tom and Mom buried Fluffy in the backyard, and put a stone with his name on it. Tom said, "Goodbye, Fluffy, goodbye. You were my best friend. I will miss you, Fluffy, I will miss you." Mom said, "Goodbye, Fluffy, goodbye. You were a sweet cat. We will remember you, Fluffy, we will remember you."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your mom, and don't leave your food or drink where your pet can get it. It could be dangerous for them, and you could lose them forever.

One day, a naughty boy named Tom wanted to have some fun. He saw a big basket of apples on a cart near his house. He thought it would be funny to drop the apples on the people in the village. He climbed on the cart and grabbed an apple.

"Hey, Tom, what are you doing?" his friend Lily asked. She was walking by with her dog.

"I'm going to drop apples on the people. It will be fun!" Tom said with a grin.

"No, Tom, that's not fun. That's mean. The people need the apples to eat. And the farmer worked hard to grow them. You should not drop them." Lily said.

But Tom did not listen. He threw an apple at a man who was carrying a basket of bread. The apple hit the man on the head and made him drop the bread. The man was angry and shouted at Tom.

"Tom, you naughty boy! How dare you drop an apple on me! You ruined my bread! Go away before I tell your mother!" the man said.

Tom was scared and ran away. He saw another apple and threw it at a woman who was knitting a scarf. The apple hit the woman on the hand and made her drop the scarf. The woman was sad and cried.

"Tom, you naughty boy! How dare you drop an apple on me! You ruined my scarf! It took me a long time to make it. Go away before I tell your father!" the woman said.

Tom was sorry and ran away. He saw one more apple and threw it at a girl who was playing with a doll. The apple hit the girl on the face and made her drop the doll. The girl was hurt and screamed.

"Tom, you naughty boy! How dare you drop an apple on me! You hurt me and my doll! Go away before I tell your teacher!" the girl said.

Tom was ashamed and ran away. He had no more apples to throw. He realized he had been very naughty and had made a lot of people angry, sad and hurt. He wished he had not dropped the apples. He wished he had listened to Lily. He wished he had been nice.

He went back to the cart and saw the farmer. The farmer was looking for his apples. He saw Tom and frowned.

"Tom, you naughty boy! Did you drop my apples on the people? Do you know how much trouble you caused? You owe me an apology and a help. Come with me and pick up the apples. And then you have to say sorry to the people. And then you have to go home and think about what you did." the farmer said.

Tom nodded and followed the farmer. He picked up the apples and said sorry to the people. He went home and thought about what he did. He decided he would never drop apples on the people again. He decided he would be a good boy from now on. He learned his lesson.

One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a red shirt and a big smile. He came to their ship and said, "Hi, I'm Ben. Can I play with you?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They did not know Ben. They did not like to share their ship. Tom said, "No, you can't. This is our ship. Go away."

Ben was sad. He said, "But I like pirates. I have a coin. It is shiny and gold. It can be your treasure. Can I add it to your map?"

Lily liked shiny things. She said, "Let me see your coin." She took it from Ben and looked at it. It was very pretty. She said, "This is a nice coin. Maybe you can play with us. But you have to be a weak pirate. You have to do what we say."

Ben nodded. He said, "OK, I can be a weak pirate. I just want to have fun." He put on a hat and a sword and followed Tom and Lily.

They played for a while. They dug holes and fought monsters and sang songs. Ben was a good pirate. He did what Tom and Lily said. He was happy.

But then, a big dog came to the park. It saw the box and the coin and the hats and the swords. It barked and ran to them. It wanted to play too.

Tom and Lily were scared. They dropped their swords and ran away. They left the box and the coin and the hats behind.

But Ben was not scared. He picked up his coin and his sword and faced the dog. He said, "Go away, dog. This is our ship. You can't have our treasure." He waved his sword and made a loud noise.

The dog was surprised. It stopped and looked at Ben. It did not like loud noises. It turned and ran away.

Tom and Lily came back. They saw Ben and the dog and the ship. They were amazed. They said, "Wow, Ben. You are not a weak pirate. You are a brave pirate. You saved our ship and our treasure. You are our friend."

Ben smiled. He said, "Thank you, Tom and Lily. You are my friends too. Can we play pirate again?"

They nodded. They said, "Yes, we can. You can add your coin to our map. You can be a strong pirate with us. We can have fun together."

They hugged and laughed and played pirate. They were happy.

"Yes, he will," Lily says. "And maybe he will let us play with it too. It looks very interesting."

He said he had a surprise for her. He took her to a special area where she could see the hippo up close. He said she could not touch the hippo, but she could talk to him and watch him play.

The end.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the big park. There were many trees and flowers and swings and slides. But there was one tree that they did not like. It was a big oak tree that was very old and grumpy. It had no leaves and no fruits and it always looked angry.

One day, Ben and Lily decided to rock on the swing near the oak tree. They pushed each other and laughed and had fun. But the oak tree did not like their noise. It shook its branches and made a loud sound.

"Stop it, stop it, you silly children!" the oak tree said. "You are bothering me. Go away and play somewhere else."

Ben and Lily were scared and surprised. They had never heard a tree talk before. They looked at the oak tree and saw its mean face.

"Who are you?" Ben asked. "Why are you so grumpy?"

"I am the oak tree, the oldest and wisest in the park," the oak tree said. "I am grumpy because I am lonely and tired. I have seen many things and I have no friends. You children are noisy and rude and you don't respect me."

Ben and Lily felt sorry for the oak tree. They did not want to make it sad. They thought of a way to cheer it up.

"Maybe you need a hug," Lily said. "We can be your friends. We can tell you stories and sing you songs and rock with you on the swing."

The oak tree was surprised and curious. It had never had a hug or a friend or a song before. It wondered what it would feel like.

"Really?" the oak tree asked. "You would do that for me?"

"Yes, we would," Ben and Lily said. "Come on, let's try."

They got off the swing and ran to the oak tree. They wrapped their arms around its trunk and gave it a big hug. They felt its bark and its warmth and its heartbeat. They told it stories about their family and their pets and their dreams. They sang it songs about the sun and the moon and the stars. They invited it to rock with them on the swing and they held its branches and made it move.

The oak tree felt something new and strange and wonderful. It felt happy and loved and alive. It smiled and laughed and thanked them.

"Thank you, thank you, you kind children," the oak tree said. "You have made me happy. You are my friends. You can play with me anytime you want."

Ben and Lily were happy too. They had made a new friend. They hugged the oak tree again and said goodbye.

"Goodbye, oak tree," they said. "We will come back soon. We love you."

They ran back to the swing and rocked and rocked and rocked. The oak tree watched them and smiled and rocked with them. They were all happy.

Sara and Ben are playing with blocks. They want to make a big tower. Sara has a red block. She puts it on top of the tower. Ben has a blue block. He tries to put it on top of the red block, but it does not fit.

"No, Ben, no!" Sara says. "The blue block is too big. It does not fit. The tower will fall down."

"But I want to use the blue block," Ben says. "It is my favorite block. It is so pretty."

Sara and Ben start to argue. They pull the blocks from each other. The tower falls down. The blocks make a loud noise. Mom hears the noise. She comes to see what is wrong.

"What are you doing, Sara and Ben?" Mom asks. "Why are you fighting? Why did you break the tower?"

Sara and Ben look at Mom. They feel sorry. They do not want to fight. They want to play.

"We are sorry, Mom," Sara and Ben say. "We wanted to make a big tower, but our blocks did not fit. Sara had a red block and I had a blue block. We both wanted to use our blocks."

Mom smiles. She hugs Sara and Ben. She says, "I understand. You both love your blocks. But sometimes you have to share and take turns. You can make a big tower together, if you use different blocks. Look, I have a treat for you. I made some cookies. They are in the kitchen. Do you want some?"

Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, please, Mom. We love cookies. Thank you, Mom."

Mom says, "You are welcome, Sara and Ben. But first, you have to clean up the blocks. Put them in the box. Then you can have a cookie."

Sara and Ben agree. They pick up the blocks. They put them in the box. They say, "We are done, Mom. Can we have a cookie now?"

Mom says, "Yes, you can. Come to the kitchen. I have a red cookie for Sara and a blue cookie for Ben. They are both yummy. They fit in your mouth. Enjoy your treat."

Sara and Ben run to the kitchen. They see the cookies. They are happy. They say, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best. We love you."

Mom says, "I love you too, Sara and Ben. You are my sweeties. Now, eat your cookies and play nicely."

But Mom says she has to wear her coat. It is cold and windy outside. Mom says she will get sick if she does not wear her coat. Mom puts the coat on Lily and zips it up.

"No, no, no!" Lily cries. She tries to unzip her coat. She wants to take it off. She does not like how it feels. She does not like how it looks.

"Lily, stop that!" Mom says. She holds Lily's hand and walks to the car. "We are going to the park. You will have fun there. You will see your friends. You will play on the swings and the slide. You will like your coat when you are there. It will keep you warm and cozy."

Lily does not listen. She still hates her coat. She pulls on the zipper. She makes it open. She feels the cold air on her skin. She shivers. She feels a drop of rain on her nose. She looks up. She sees dark clouds in the sky. She hears thunder. She sees lightning.

Lily is scared. She does not like the rain. She does not like the thunder. She does not like the lightning. She wants to go back home. She wants to be safe and dry.

She looks at Mom. She sees Mom's coat. It is blue and soft. It is not too big and not too red. It looks nice. It looks warm.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. Today, they want to race their cars on the road.

"Ready, set, go!" Tom says. He pushes his red car with all his might. His car is very fast and shiny. He wants to win the race.

Sam pushes his blue car, but his car is slow and old. He tries to catch up with Tom, but Tom is too far ahead. Sam feels sad and angry. He thinks Tom is not fair.

"Ha ha, I win!" Tom says. He stops his car and turns around. He sees Sam far behind. He laughs at Sam. He thinks he is better than Sam.

Sam stops his car too. He does not want to play with Tom anymore. He thinks Tom is mean and rude. He picks up his car and walks away.

"Hey, where are you going?" Tom asks. He does not understand why Sam is leaving. He thinks Sam is a sore loser.

"I don't want to play with you," Sam says. "You are not a good friend. You only care about winning. You don't care about having fun."

Tom feels confused and sorry. He realizes he was wrong. He did not think about Sam's feelings. He did not share his cars. He did not say nice things.

"Wait, Sam, I'm sorry," Tom says. He runs after Sam. He wants to make up with Sam. He wants to be a good friend.

"Sorry for what?" Sam asks. He stops and looks at Tom.

"Sorry for being mean and rude," Tom says. "Sorry for laughing at you. Sorry for not sharing my cars. Sorry for not caring about having fun."

Sam looks at Tom. He sees Tom is sincere. He feels happy and relieved. He forgives Tom.

"It's okay, Tom," Sam says. "I'm sorry for being sad and angry. I know you like fast cars. I like slow cars. We can play with both."

Tom smiles and nods. He gives Sam his red car. Sam gives Tom his blue car. They hug and make up.

They go back to the road. They push their cars together. They don't care who wins. They only care about having fun.

The moral of the story is: Be a good friend. Don't be mean and rude. Share your toys. Care about others' feelings. Have fun.

"No, no, no!" Lily said. "I don't want medicine!"

"Lily, please, you have to take it. It will help you heal fast. Don't you want to play with your toys and your friends again?" Mommy said.

Lily shook her head. She hid under the blanket. She did not want to play. She just wanted to be left alone.

Mommy sighed. She knew Lily was scared and stubborn. She had an idea. She went to the kitchen and came back with a glass of juice and a cookie.

"Lily, look what I have for you. Some juice and a cookie. But you can only have them if you take your medicine first. How about that?" Mommy said.

Lily peeked from the blanket. She saw the juice and the cookie. They looked yummy. She loved juice and cookies. She wanted to have them. But she still did not want to take the medicine.

"Can I have the juice and the cookie without the medicine?" Lily asked.

Mommy shook her head. "No, Lily, you can't. The medicine is important. It will make you strong and healthy. The juice and the cookie are just a treat. You have to do the hard thing before the easy thing. That's how you grow up and learn."

Lily thought about it. She did not like the hard thing. But she wanted to grow up and learn. She wanted to be strong and healthy. She wanted to make Mommy happy. She decided to be brave and try the medicine.

"Okay, Mommy, I will take the medicine. But only a little bit," Lily said.

Mommy smiled. She gave Lily a hug and a kiss. She gave her the spoon with the medicine. Lily closed her eyes and opened her mouth. She swallowed the medicine. It was bitter and yucky. She made a face.

"Good girl, Lily! You did it! I'm so proud of you!" Mommy said. She gave Lily the juice and the cookie. Lily drank the juice and ate the cookie. They were sweet and yummy. She smiled.

"Thank you, Mommy. The juice and the cookie are good. The medicine is not good. But I feel better already," Lily said.

Mommy hugged Lily again. She tucked her in the bed. She sang her a lullaby. Lily fell asleep. She dreamed of playing with her toys and her friends again.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes we have to do things we don't like to get things we do like. We have to be brave and listen to our parents. They know what's best for us. They love us and want us to be happy.

One day, Sam wanted to fly his kite by himself. He asked his dad if he could go to the park alone. His dad said no, it was not safe. He said he would go with him later. But Sam did not listen. He was foolish. He took his kite and ran to the park.

But then, he heard a loud honk. He looked down and saw a big truck on the road. The truck was coming fast. The truck had a long trailer. The trailer had a sign that said "Danger: Explosives". Sam's kite was flying right over the trailer. The string was about to touch the sign.

Sam was scared. He tried to pull his kite back. But it was too late. The string touched the sign. There was a big boom. The trailer blew up. The kite blew up. Sam flew off the hill. He landed on the grass. He was hurt. He cried.

His dad heard the boom. He ran to the park. He saw Sam on the ground. He saw the smoke and the fire. He was angry and sad. He hugged Sam and said, "Why did you do that? Why did you not listen to me? I told you it was not safe. You were foolish. You could have died."

His dad said, "Yes, son. We can still fly kites together. But not today. Today, we have to go to the hospital. You need to get checked. You have some cuts and bruises. And you have a big lesson to learn."

"Are you okay, kids?" Mom asked.

Lily and Ben nodded. They were scared and sad.

"Sure, you can play with them," said Timmy, pouring the cars into Billy's hands.

But Billy wasn't kind like Timmy. He took the metal cars and ran away. Timmy was sad and cried.

The next day, Timmy saw Billy playing with the metal cars in the park. Timmy went to get his cars back, but Billy wouldn't give them back. They started to fight over the cars, and Timmy got hurt.

Timmy went home with bruises and cuts, and his mom asked him what happened. Timmy told his mom about Billy and the metal cars. His mom was angry and called Billy's parents. Billy got in trouble for taking Timmy's toys.

From then on, Timmy only played with kind friends who wouldn't take his toys. The end.

But then, Ducky started to feel a tickle in his nose. He knew he was going to sneeze! And sure enough, a big "achoo!" came out of his beak. The other animals in the pond looked at him and laughed. Ducky felt a little embarrassed, but he couldn't help it. He was just a sneezy little duck.

After his sneeze, Ducky decided to swim some more. He saw a family of frogs on a lily pad and paddled over to say hello. They were very friendly and Ducky had a great time playing with them. From then on, Ducky loved to swim and explore the pond, and he didn't mind if he sneezed every now and then.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, Max's collar got dirty and he didn't like it. He went to his friend Bella and asked her, "Bella, can you help me clean my collar?"

Bella answered, "Sure Max, I can help you. Let's go to the river and wash it." But when they got to the river, they saw that the water was too dirty. Max got sad and said, "Now what do we do? My collar is still dirty."

Just then, they saw a kind lady walking by. Max went up to her and asked, "Excuse me, can you help me clean my collar?" The lady smiled and said, "Of course, I can help you. Let's go to my house and wash it." Max was happy and thanked the lady. When they got to her house, she washed Max's collar and it became clean again. Max was so happy and thanked the lady again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet lived on a hill with many other little birds. One day, Tweet saw a lonely bird named Chirp. Chirp was worried because he didn't have any friends to play with. Tweet went to Chirp and said, "Do you want to join us on the hill? We can play together!" Chirp was very happy and joined the other little birds on the hill.

The little birds played together all day long. They sang songs, flew around, and had lots of fun. Chirp was no longer worried because he had new friends to play with. At the end of the day, Tweet said, "I am happy we could all play together. Remember, it's always nice to make new friends and include them in our games." All the little birds agreed and chirped happily as they went to sleep.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and include others who may be feeling left out. When we make new friends, we all have more fun together!

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play on the farm. They liked to run, jump, and sing with the animals. One day, they saw a new animal on the farm. It was big and brown, with long ears and a furry tail. It looked like a horse, but not quite.

"What is that?" Tom asked.

"That is a mule," Lily said. "Dad said he is here to help with the work. He can carry heavy things and pull the cart."

"Can we play with him?" Tom asked.

"I don't know. Let's ask Dad," Lily said.

They ran to the farmhouse and found Dad. He was busy fixing the fence.

"Dad, Dad, can we play with the mule?" they asked.

Dad smiled and put down his tools.

"Sure, you can play with the mule, but be careful. He is very strong and sometimes stubborn. He might not do what you want him to do. And don't go near his back legs. He might kick if he gets scared or angry."

"Okay, Dad, we will be careful," they said.

They ran back to the field where the mule was. He was eating some grass and looked bored.

"Hello, mule," Tom said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The mule lifted his head and looked at them. He made a loud noise that sounded like "hee-haw".

"Wow, he can talk!" Lily said.

"No, he can't. That's just how he says hello," Tom said.

They went closer to the mule and tried to pet him. He let them touch his ears and his nose, but he moved away when they tried to touch his tail.

"He doesn't like that," Lily said.

"Maybe he likes this," Tom said. He picked up a stick and threw it. "Fetch, mule, fetch!"

The mule watched the stick fly and then looked at Tom. He made another noise that sounded like "hee-haw".

"He doesn't want to fetch," Lily said.

"Maybe he likes this," Tom said. He ran around the mule and tried to make him chase him. "Come on, mule, come on!"

The mule watched Tom run and then looked at Lily. He made another noise that sounded like "hee-haw".

"He doesn't want to chase," Lily said.

"Maybe he likes this," Tom said. He climbed on the mule's back and tried to make him move. "Giddy up, mule, giddy up!"

The mule felt Tom on his back and then looked at Lily. He made another noise that sounded like "hee-haw". Then he shook his back and threw Tom off.

"Ouch!" Tom said. He landed on the grass and rubbed his head.

"He doesn't want to ride," Lily said.

They looked at the mule and saw him smiling. He was playful, but in his own way. He liked to tease them and make them laugh.

They laughed too and decided to play something else. They liked the mule, even if he was stubborn. He was a good friend.

Ben nods and smiles. He likes cats. He says, "Your cat is very nice. It is orange, like a carrot. Can I draw a carrot for your cat?"

Lily says, "Yes, please. My cat likes carrots. They are good for her eyes. Can I draw a bowl for your fish?"

Ben says, "Yes, please. My fish likes bowls. They are good for his fins. We can draw a lot of things for our animals."

Tom and Sue are sad. They cry. They say they love Max. They say they will not play with the pick again. They say they will be good. They hope Max will be okay. They wait for Mom and Max to come back.

They heard the car in the driveway and ran to the door. They greeted mom and dad with hugs and kisses. They told them about the thunder and the story. Mom and dad praised Ben for being a good brother and Anna for being a brave sister. They said they were proud of them and that they loved them.

They all went to the kitchen and had cookies and milk. They talked and laughed and enjoyed being together. The thunder was still there, but it didn't bother them anymore. They knew they had each other to comfort them.

One day, Lily sees a new zoom car in the toy store. It is red and shiny and has a big button on the side. The sign says it is a powerful zoom car that can do tricks and flips. Lily wants to get the powerful zoom car, but it is very expensive.

She decides to get the powerful zoom car by herself. She waits until her mom is busy and sneaks the zoom car into her backpack. She thinks she is very clever and nobody will notice.

But when she gets home, she finds out that her mom knows everything. Her mom saw the security camera in the toy store and saw Lily take the zoom car without paying. Her mom is very disappointed and angry. She says Lily has to return the zoom car and say sorry to the store owner. She also says Lily has to give away some of her zoom cars to other kids who don't have any.

Lily feels very ashamed and sorry. She realizes she did a bad thing and hurt her mom and the store owner. She also realizes that having a powerful zoom car is not worth losing her mom's trust and love.

She returns the zoom car and apologizes to the store owner. She also gives away some of her zoom cars to other kids who are happy to get them. She learns that stealing is wrong and sharing is good. One day, he saw a big window in his room. He thought it would be fun to fly his plane outside. He opened the window and threw his plane. He watched it soar in the sky. He felt happy and proud.

But then, he saw a big bird. The bird saw the plane and thought it was a snack. It flew towards the plane and grabbed it with its beak. It flew away with the plane. Tom felt sad and angry. He wanted his plane back.

Lisa loved strawberries. She liked to pick them from the garden with her mom and dad. She liked to wash them in the sink and eat them with cream. She liked to make them into jam and cake. But most of all, she liked to put them in her mouth and feel them burst with juice.

One day, Lisa saw a big, red, shiny strawberry on the kitchen table. It was the biggest strawberry she had ever seen. She wanted to eat it right away. But her mom said, "No, Lisa, that strawberry is for later. We are going to have a special guest for dinner. He is a very nice man who likes strawberries too. You can share it with him."

Lisa was sad. She did not want to share the strawberry. She wanted it all for herself. She thought, maybe I can hide it somewhere and eat it later. She looked around the kitchen and saw a big, brown, round pot. She thought, that is a good place to put the strawberry. No one will find it there. She climbed on a chair and reached for the pot. She lifted the lid and put the strawberry inside. Then she put the lid back and got down from the chair. She smiled and ran to her room.

That evening, Lisa heard the doorbell ring. She ran to the door and saw her mom and dad greet the special guest. He was a tall, chubby, friendly man with a big beard and a red suit. He had a big bag on his shoulder. He said, "Hello, Lisa, I am Santa Claus. I have come to bring you some presents. But first, I am very hungry. Do you have anything to eat?"

Lisa's mom said, "Of course, we have a delicious dinner for you. Come, sit at the table. We have soup, salad, bread, cheese, and a big, red, shiny strawberry for dessert. Lisa picked it from the garden herself. She loves strawberries."

Lisa felt a pang of guilt. She remembered the strawberry she had put in the pot. She wondered if it was still there. She hoped no one would notice. She followed her mom and dad and Santa to the table. She sat next to Santa and smiled nervously.

Her mom brought the soup and poured it into the bowls. She gave one to Santa and said, "Here you go, Santa, enjoy your soup. It is very hot and tasty. It will warm you up on this cold night."

Santa thanked her and lifted the spoon to his mouth. He blew on the soup and took a sip. Then he made a funny face and spat out the soup. He said, "Blech! What is this? There is something in my soup. It is sweet and squishy and red. It is a strawberry!"

Lisa gasped and turned red. She knew it was her strawberry. She had put it in the pot. She had forgotten to take it out. She had ruined the soup. She had ruined the dinner. She had ruined the night. She felt very bad. She said, "I'm sorry, Santa, I'm sorry, mom, I'm sorry, dad. It was my strawberry. I put it in the pot. I wanted to eat it later. I did not want to share it. I was selfish. Please forgive me."

Santa looked at Lisa and smiled. He said, "Don't worry, Lisa, it's okay. I forgive you. Everyone makes mistakes. You are a good girl. You told the truth. You learned your lesson. Sharing is caring. And I have a surprise for you. In my bag, I have a whole basket of strawberries for you. You can have them all. You can eat them, share them, or put them wherever you want. But please, not in the soup."

Lisa smiled and hugged Santa. She said, "Thank you, Santa, thank you, thank you. You are very nice. You are very generous. You are the best. I love you. And I love strawberries."

Her mom and dad smiled and hugged Lisa too. They said, "We love you too, Lisa. You are our sweet, brave, smart girl. And we love strawberries too. Let's have some for dessert. And maybe some cream. And maybe some cake. And maybe some jam. And maybe some more soup. But without strawberries."

They all laughed and enjoyed their dinner. They had a wonderful night. And Lisa never put strawberries in the pot again.

One day, Lily saw a big boy in the park. He had a big bike and a big hat. He looked at Lily and said, "What is that? A flute? That is a baby toy. You are a baby. I dare you to play the flute for me. I bet you can't."

Lily felt scared and angry. She was not a baby. She could play the flute very well. She said, "I can play the flute. I am not a baby. I will play the flute for you."

Tom and Sue wanted to play a game. They had a big ball and two baskets. They decided to play ball-basket. The rule was to carry the ball and put it in the basket. The one who put the most balls in the basket would win. They called it victory.

Tom was fat and slow. Sue was thin and fast. Tom thought he could not win. Sue thought she could win easily. She said to Tom, "You are too fat to carry the ball. I will win and have victory. You will lose and be sad."

Tom felt bad. He wanted to win. He wanted to have victory. He wanted to make Sue sad. He had an idea. He said to Sue, "Let's make the game more fun. Let's put the baskets far away. The farther the basket, the more points you get. Do you agree?"

Sue agreed. She thought she could run faster than Tom. She thought she could carry the ball farther than Tom. She thought she could get more points than Tom. She said to Tom, "OK, let's do that. But you will still lose. I will still win. I will still have victory."

They started the game. Sue ran fast with the ball. She carried the ball to the farthest basket. She put the ball in the basket. She got many points. She was happy. She said to Tom, "See? I told you. You are too fat to carry the ball. You are too slow to run. You will never win. You will never have victory."

Tom did not run fast. He did not carry the ball to the farthest basket. He carried the ball to the nearest basket. He put the ball in the basket. He got few points. He was not happy. He said to Sue, "You are right. I am too fat to carry the ball. I am too slow to run. I will never win. I will never have victory."

They played for a long time. Sue always ran fast and carried the ball far. Tom always ran slow and carried the ball near. Sue always got many points. Tom always got few points. Sue always laughed. Tom always cried.

But then something happened. Sue got tired. She ran out of breath. She could not run fast anymore. She could not carry the ball far anymore. She could not get many points anymore. She was not happy anymore.

Tom did not get tired. He had a lot of breath. He could still run slow and carry the ball near. He could still get few points. He was not sad anymore.

They played until the end. They counted the points. Tom had more points than Sue. Tom won. Tom had victory. Sue lost. Sue did not have victory.

Tom was happy. He said to Sue, "See? I told you. You are too thin to carry the ball. You are too fast to run. You got tired. You lost. You did not have victory."

Sue was sad. She said to Tom, "You are right. I am too thin to carry the ball. I am too fast to run. I got tired. I lost. I did not have victory."

Tom and Sue learned a lesson. They learned that being fat or thin does not matter. They learned that being fast or slow does not matter. They learned that being smart and fair matters. They learned that being kind and friendly matters. They learned that playing for fun matters. They learned that sharing victory matters.

They hugged each other. They said sorry. They said thank you. They said well done. They said let's play again. They said let's be friends. They were happy. They had victory.

"Neigh!" Lily said, stretching her neck. "I am the tallest of the animals!"

"Lily, what's wrong?" Sam asked, seeing her face.

"I need to go to the bathroom, Sam," Lily said, holding her tummy.

"Okay, let's go," Sam said, getting off the couch. "But you have to be fast. Mommy said we have to clean up our toys soon."

They ran to the bathroom, but when they got there, they saw a sign on the door. It said "Out of order".

"What does that mean, Sam?" Lily asked, looking at the sign.

Sam tried to read the sign, but he did not know all the words. He only knew "out" and "order".

"I don't know, Lily," Sam said, scratching his head. "Maybe it means the bathroom is broken."

"Broken?" Lily said, feeling more urgent. "But I need to go now, Sam!"

Sam looked around and saw another door across the hall. It had a picture of a toilet on it.

"Look, Lily, there's another bathroom!" Sam said, pointing to the door. "Maybe we can use that one."

They ran to the other door and opened it. It was a bathroom, but it looked different from the one they usually used. It had a big tub, a sink, and a toilet, but the toilet was very high and had a chain hanging from the ceiling.

"What is this, Sam?" Lily asked, looking at the toilet.

Sam had never seen a toilet like that before. He did not know how to use it.

"I don't know, Lily," Sam said, looking at the chain. "Maybe you have to pull the chain to flush the toilet."

"Flush?" Lily said, not understanding.

Sam tried to explain. "Flush means to make the water go away after you use the toilet."

"Oh," Lily said, nodding. "But how do I get up there, Sam? The toilet is too high for me."

Sam looked around and saw a small stool next to the tub. He had an idea.

"Here, Lily, use this stool," Sam said, moving the stool to the toilet. "You can stand on it and reach the toilet."

Lily climbed on the stool and sat on the toilet. She was glad she made it in time.

"Thank you, Sam," Lily said, smiling.

"You're welcome, Lily," Sam said, smiling back.

They heard a knock on the door. It was Mommy.

"Sam, Lily, are you in there?" Mommy asked.

"Yes, Mommy, we're in here," Sam said.

"Are you okay?" Mommy asked.

"Yes, Mommy, we're okay," Lily said.

"We're using the other bathroom, Mommy," Sam said.

"The other bathroom?" Mommy said, sounding surprised. "Why are you using the other bathroom?"

Sam and Lily looked at each other. They did not know how to explain the sign, the broken bathroom, and the high toilet to Mommy.

They decided to say the simplest thing they could think of.

"Because we had to go, Mommy," Sam and Lily said together.

She put the turkey in a big pan and covered it with foil. She put it in the oven and turned it on. She set the timer.

"Can we watch the turkey, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Sure, you can. But be careful, the oven is hot. Don't touch it. Just look through the glass," Mom said.

Tom and Jen sat on the floor and watched the turkey. They saw it change from brown to golden. They smelled the delicious aroma. They heard the timer beep.

"Is it ready, Mom?" Jen asked.

"Yes, it is. Let's take it out and carve it. Then we can eat it with some mashed potatoes and gravy and cranberry sauce. Doesn't that sound good?" Mom said.

"It sounds great, Mom!" Tom and Jen said.

They helped Mom set the table and bring the food. They sat down and said grace. They thanked God for the turkey and the rain and the fun. They ate and enjoyed the meal. They were happy and full.

They forgot about the gloomy day. They had a turkey day.

Sam was a bald man who liked to polish his car. He had a big red car that shone in the sun. He used a soft cloth and a bottle of wax to make his car look nice.

One day, he was polishing his car in his driveway when he saw a little girl walking by. She had long brown hair and a pink dress. She stopped and looked at his car with her big eyes.

"Hello, little girl," Sam said. "Do you like my car?"

"Yes, it is very pretty," the girl said. "But why are you bald? Where is your hair?"

Sam smiled and touched his head. "I don't have any hair," he said. "It fell off a long time ago. But I don't mind. I like being bald."

The girl tilted her head and frowned. "But don't you get cold?" she asked. "Or sunburned?"

Sam laughed and shook his head. "No, I don't get cold or sunburned," he said. "I wear a hat when it is cold or sunny. See, I have a hat right here." He showed her a blue hat with a star on it.

The girl nodded and smiled. "That is a nice hat," she said. "Can I try it on?"

Sam nodded and handed her the hat. She put it on her head and giggled. "It is too big for me," she said. "But it is fun."

Sam smiled and said, "You look very cute with the hat. Do you want to keep it?"

The girl looked at him with her big eyes and said, "Really? Can I?"

Sam nodded and said, "Sure, you can. It is a gift from me to you. Just remember to polish it once in a while."

The girl hugged him and said, "Thank you, bald man. You are very nice. I will polish the hat and take good care of it."

Sam hugged her back and said, "You are very welcome, little girl. You are very sweet. I hope you enjoy the hat."

They waved goodbye and the girl walked away with the hat on her head. Sam went back to polishing his car, feeling happy and warm. He liked making new friends.

Lily hated socks. She hated how they felt on her feet, how they made her toes hot and sweaty, how they sometimes had holes or strings. She hated how her mom always told her to wear socks, even when it was sunny and warm outside. She hated how her dad always checked her socks, and made her change them if they were dirty or wet.

One day, Lily decided to hide all her socks. She took them from her drawer, from the laundry basket, from the closet. She stuffed them under her bed, behind her books, in her toy box. She thought she was very clever, and no one would find them. She smiled and ran to the kitchen, where her mom was making breakfast.

"Lily, where are your socks?" her mom asked, looking at her bare feet.

"I don't know," Lily lied, shrugging her shoulders.

"You don't know? Did you lose them? Did you forget them?" her mom asked, frowning.

"No, I don't know," Lily repeated, feeling a little scared.

"Lily, what is this?" her mom asked, holding up a sock.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was very poor and had nothing to play with. She sat sadly on the ground.

Suddenly, she saw a stick on the ground. She picked it up and started playing with it. She pointed the stick like it was a wand, pretending that she had magical powers.

As Jane was playing, she saw a man walking towards her. He was a very rich man. He smiled at Jane and said, "My, my! You have a very special stick."

The rich man reached into his pocket and pulled out a bag of coins. He gave the bag to Jane and said, "here, take this. Now you can buy something special with your stick!"

Jane thanked the rich man and said goodbye. She ran all the way home, very excited to spend her money!

Jane was so happy that she had been given something so special simply by pointing her stick. From that day on, she always carried her stick with her everywhere she went.

Mary was walking in the park. She saw a fierce tiger in front of her and became very scared. The tiger opened its mouth and said, "I'm so hungry, I'm going to eat you!"

Mary was so scared that she started to cry. She thought of an idea. She quickly looked around, saw a vase and said, "Let's eat this, you must be very hungry!"

The tiger became curious. He looked at the vase and said, "What's this?" Mary explained, "This is a vase. It's made of clay and looks like a bowl. We can eat the clay inside."

The tiger had never heard of eating clay before, so he was not sure what to do. He thought it over and eventually agreed to try it. As they ate the clay from inside the vase, the tiger was surprised how tasty it was! 

The tiger thanked Mary and said "You saved my life today. I won't be so fierce next time." Mary smiled and said, "That's Okay. Just remember to be a good tiger."

Once upon a time there was a little bear who lived in the woods. The bear was very clever, he always knew what to do in any situation.

One day, the bear went for an adventure and came across a stream. He thought about crossing it but he did not know how. Just then, a rabbit hopped by.

The bear asked the rabbit, "Please help me cross the stream!" The rabbit said, "Well, I can't cross it, but I know the frog can help you."

The bear thanked the rabbit and he went looking for the frog. He found the frog and asked him the same question. The frog replied, "I can help you with remembering. What you need to remember is to jump from one rock to the other."

The bear followed the frog's advice and managed to cross the stream! He thanked the frog and was on his way.

The moral of the story is that remembering helps us solve many problems. We should always remember the things that will help us and be clever.

Once upon a time, there was a poor farmer. His farm was filled with sheep. He was very sad and had no friends.

One day, he was sitting in his barn, and he saw something outside the window. He looked closer and noticed that all of his sheep were scattering in all directions.

He ran outside, shouting, "Come back, my sheep! Where are you going?"

A nearby sheep replied, "We're searching for green pastures so we can eat. We're too poor to have enough food here!"

The farmer thought for a moment and then smiled. "Don't worry, my sheep. I will find a way to help us. Follow me!"

The farmer then dug deep into the ground, and found something strange. He found enough grass for all the sheep to eat.

The farmer said, "See, I told you that I would help you. We're not so poor anymore!"

The sheep were very happy. They ate the grass and smiled at the farmer before scurrying off.

From that day on, the farmer was never poor again. He and the sheep lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there lived a jellyfish in the sea. He was a happy little creature and loved to explore the big deep blue. One day, he met a cheap crab walking along the bottom of the ocean. The crab was mean and kept teasing the jellyfish because of his soft, squishy body. The jellyfish didn't like this at all and got very angry.

He called out to the crab, "Please stop! That's not nice!" But the crab didn't listen. He kept on teasing the jellyfish and calling him names.

The jellyfish was so upset that he began to cry. He wished he could do something about the crab's meanness. But he couldn't think of anything. Just then, an amazing thing happened. Suddenly, all the fish around them stopped swimming and the crab stopped teasing.

The jellyfish looked at all the fish. He couldn't believe what he was seeing. The fish were smiling at him, and the crab too. Then, one of the fish spoke to him. "It's ok, jellyfish," the fish said. "It's ok to forgive."

The jellyfish understood. His anger melted away and he smiled at the crab. He knew what the fish meant. He could forgive the crab and move on. And that's just what he did. From then on, the jellyfish and the crab were friends, and they never argued again!

Once upon a time, there was a bear who found a fake flower. He liked it so much he decided to take it home and show his family. He was on the way home when he passed a laundry with a colorful sign that said "Clothes Belong Here!". He gasped as he saw a pile of laundry on a chair and thought it looked cozy and warm. 

The bear asked the laundry, "What are you doing here?" 

The laundry replied, "I am here to stay safe and warm." 

The bear said, "But this is not where clothes belong. They belong on hangers!" 

The laundry just laughed and said, "This pile of clothes may look like it doesn't belong, but it's actually a fake pile of clothes that nobody needs. So, here I stay nice and cozy while nobody needs me !" 

The bear thanked the laundry for the wisdom and gave it the fake flower. He said, "I'm happy you are safe and warm."

The laundry smiled and said, "Thank you for the gift. I'll keep it here with me forever!" 

The bear smiled and continued his journey home with the new knowledge that things don't always have to look the way they should, and sometimes fake things can help us stay safe and warm.

Mom said, "Lily, you have to wash now. It's almost lunch time. You can play with your cars later. Come on, let's go to the bathroom." Mom took Lily's hand and led her to the sink.

Lily was not happy. She made a noisy fuss. She cried and kicked and said, "No, no, no!" Mom said, "Lily, please calm down. Washing is good for you. It makes you clean and healthy. Look, I have your favorite soap. It smells like strawberries. And your towel is soft and pink. Don't you like them?"

Lily looked at the soap and the towel. She liked them. She liked strawberries and pink. She stopped crying and said, "OK, mom, I will wash. But can I bring one car with me?" Mom said, "Sure, you can bring one car. But be careful not to get it wet. Which car do you want to bring?"

Lily thought for a moment. She looked at her cars. She picked the blue one. It was her favorite. She said, "I want to bring this one. It's fast and shiny. Can I wash it too?" Mom said, "No, Lily, you can't wash your car. It's not a real car. It's a model car. If you wash it, it will get ruined. You can only wash your hands and face. OK?"

Lily said, "OK, mom, I understand. I will not wash my car. I will only wash me. And then I will play with my car again." Mom said, "That's a good girl. Now let's wash and have lunch. And then you can play with your cars as much as you want." Lily smiled and said, "OK, mom, I love you." Mom said, "I love you too, Lily." And they washed and had lunch and played with the cars.

Lily was hungry. She wanted some milk and a cookie. She went to the kitchen and looked for the milk. She saw a big bottle on the table. She tried to reach it, but it was too high. She got a chair and climbed on it. She grabbed the bottle and pulled it down. But the bottle was too heavy. It slipped from her hand and fell on the floor. It broke and spilled milk everywhere. Lily was scared. She jumped off the chair and ran to her mom.

"Mommy, mommy, I'm sorry!" she cried. "I broke the milk!"

Mommy heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw the mess and Lily's tears. She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, sweetie. It was an accident. You didn't mean to break the milk. Are you hurt?"

Lily shook her head. "No, mommy, I'm not hurt. But I'm still hungry."

Mommy smiled and said, "Don't worry, we have more milk in the fridge. And I have some cookies for you. Come on, let's clean up this mess and then we can have a snack."

Lily nodded and said, "Thank you, mommy. I love you."

Mommy said, "I love you too, Lily. You are a good girl."
