"Oh no, the swing is broken!" Anna says. "We can't play on it anymore."

"Maybe we can fix it," Ben says. "We can find a new rope and tie it to the tree."

Anna and Ben look for a new rope. They find one in the garage. It is long and strong. They carry it to the yard.

"Can you help us, dad?" Ben asks. "We want to fix the swing."

"Sure, I can help you," dad says. "But you have to be patient. It might take some time to fix it."

Dad takes the rope and climbs the ladder. He ties one end of the rope to the tree. He ties the other end to the seat. He makes sure it is tight and safe.

"Look, the swing is fixed!" Anna says. "Thank you, dad!"

"You're welcome, Anna," dad says. "Now you can play on it again. But be careful and have fun."

One day, Anna wanted to play with Lily, but Lily did not want to play. Lily was lying on the couch, looking sleepy. Anna tried to make Lily get up by pulling her tail, but Lily only hissed and scratched Anna's hand. Anna cried and ran to her mom.

"Mom, Lily is mean! She scratched me and refused to play with me!" Anna said, showing her hand.

Mom looked at Anna's hand and gave her a hug. She put a band-aid on the scratch and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. Lily is not mean, she is just tired. Sometimes cats need to rest and be alone. You should not pull her tail, that hurts her. You should be gentle and obedient with Lily, and she will be your friend."

Anna nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. I will be gentle and obedient with Lily. Can I play with the string instead?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can play with the string. But be careful not to tangle it or lose it. And maybe later, when Lily wakes up, she will want to play with you too."

Anna said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you and I love Lily." She took the string and went to her room. She made shapes and patterns with the string on the floor. She hoped Lily would come and join her soon.

Sara was a nurse who liked to help people. She worked in a big hospital with many beds and machines. She was very organized and always knew where to find things. She wore a white dress and a hat with a red cross.

One day, a boy named Ben came to the hospital. He had a cut on his knee and it hurt a lot. He cried and held his mom's hand. Sara saw him and smiled. She said, "Hello, Ben. I am Sara, a nurse. I will help you feel better. Don't be scared."

She took him to a small room with a table and a chair. She asked him to sit on the table and lifted his leg. She cleaned his cut with a soft cloth and some water. She said, "This will make your cut clean and stop the germs. It might sting a little, but it will be over soon." Ben nodded and tried not to cry. He was brave.

Then, Sara put a band-aid on his cut and a sticker on his shirt. She said, "There, you are all done. You are a very good patient. The band-aid will protect your cut and the sticker will make you happy. Do you like it?" Ben looked at the sticker. It was a dinosaur. He liked dinosaurs. He smiled and said, "Thank you, Sara. You are a very nice nurse. The sticker is cool."

Sara hugged him and said, "You are very welcome, Ben. I am glad you like it. Now you can go home with your mom and play. But be careful and don't run too fast. You don't want to hurt your knee again." Ben nodded and said, "OK, Sara. I will be careful. Bye-bye." He waved and walked out with his mom. Sara waved back and went to help another person. She was a nurse who liked to help people.

"What does it do?" Anna asks.

"Let's find out!" Ben says. He pushes the button.

Suddenly, the rocket makes a loud noise. It shoots out gas from the back. The gas makes the slide very slippery. Anna and Ben slide down the slide very fast. They feel like they are flying. They go through the tunnel and land on a soft mat.

"Wow!" Anna says. "That was amazing!"

"That was so fun!" Ben says. "Let's do it again!"

They run back to the slide and push the button. They slide down the slide again and again. They have the best time ever. They love the new slide. It is their new favorite thing.

One night, they hear a ring. It is not a ring from the phone or the door. It is a ring from the window. They look out and see a fairy. She has wings and a wand. She smiles at them and says, "Hello, Tom and Lily. Do you want to go on an adventure?"

Tom and Lily are surprised and happy. They nod and say, "Yes, please!" The fairy flies in and sprinkles some dust on them. They feel light and floaty. The fairy says, "Hold my hands and we will fly to the fair. There are many fun things to see and do there."

Tom and Lily hold the fairy's hands and fly out of the window. They see the stars and the moon. They see the fair with bright lights and music. They see rides and games and candy. The fairy says, "You can choose what you want to do. But you have to be back before the sun comes up. Or your parents will worry."

Tom and Lily have a lot of fun at the fair. They ride the carousel and the ferris wheel. They play the ring toss and the duck pond. They eat cotton candy and popcorn. They laugh and giggle. They thank the fairy for taking them.

The fairy says, "You are welcome, Tom and Lily. You are very fair and kind. But it is time to go back now. The sun will rise soon." She flies them back to their window and tucks them in their bed. She says, "Good night, Tom and Lily. Sweet dreams." She kisses them on their cheeks and flies away.

Tom and Lily fall asleep with smiles on their faces. They dream of the fair and the fairy. They do not hear their parents come in and check on them. They do not know that the fairy left a ring on their pillow. A ring that sparkles and glows. A ring that is a gift and a memory. A ring that is magic.

One day, they decide to sort insects. They go to the garden and look for insects. They see ants, bees, butterflies, ladybugs, and more. They catch some in a jar and put them on a table. They want to sort them by how many legs they have, or how they fly, or what they eat.

But the insects do not like to be sorted. They are wild and want to be free. They buzz and crawl and flap in the jar. They try to escape and bite and sting. Lila and Sam get scared and drop the jar. The insects fly and run away.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lila cries. "A bee stung me!"

"Sorry, sorry, sorry!" Sam says. "I did not know they would be so wild!"

They run to their mom and show her their jar and their stings. Mom hugs them and puts some ice and cream on their stings. She tells them not to sort insects anymore.

"Insects are not toys," she says. "They are living things that need their space and their homes. You can look at them and learn about them, but you should not catch them and sort them. They are not happy that way."

Lila and Sam nod and say they are sorry. They promise to be kind to insects and leave them alone. They still like to sort things, but not insects. They sort other things that are not wild and do not sting.

One night, Tom was very tired. He put his toys away in his box. He said good night to his truck, his bear, and his ball. He climbed into his bed and pulled his blanket over him. He felt warm and cozy.

"Tom, are you asleep?" his mom asked. She came into his room and kissed his forehead. She turned off his light and sat on his bed.

"No, mom, I'm not asleep," Tom said. He opened his eyes and smiled at his mom.

"Yes, please, mom. Can you read me the one about the lion and the mouse?" Tom asked.

"Sure, Tom. That's a good story. It's about how to be kind and help others," his mom said. She picked up the book and opened it. She read the story to Tom in a soft voice.

Tom listened to the story. He liked the lion and the mouse. He liked how the mouse helped the lion when he was in trouble. He liked how the lion thanked the mouse and became his friend.

"Mom, can I ask you something?" Tom said.

"Of course, Tom. What is it?" his mom said.

"What does 'dead' mean?" Tom asked. He had heard that word on TV and he did not understand it.

"Dead means that something is not alive anymore. It does not breathe, or move, or feel anything. It is very sad when something is dead," his mom said.

"Like the fly I saw on the window?" Tom asked.

"Yes, like the fly. The fly was dead. It could not fly anymore," his mom said.

"Will you be dead, mom?" Tom asked.

His mom hugged him tighter. She felt a tear in her eye.

"No, Tom, I will not be dead. I will always be with you. I will always love you. You don't have to worry about that," his mom said.

"Okay, mom. I love you too. Good night, mom," Tom said.

"Good night, Tom. Sweet dreams," his mom said.

She kissed him again and put the book down. She got up and left his room. She looked back at him and smiled. He was asleep. He looked peaceful and happy. She thanked God for her son. She thanked God for her bed. She thanked God for her life.

Lily decided that she wanted to learn more about minerals, so she asked her mommy to take her to the library. At the library, she found a book about minerals and read all about them. Now, Lily could recognize many different minerals and was excited to find more!

Once upon a time, there was a little bee who lived in a hive. The bee was very happy because she had a lot of friends and they loved to play together. One day, the bee went to bathe in a pond near the hive. She loved to splash around in the water and feel clean.

But while the bee was bathing, she saw a beautiful flower in the distance. It was so brilliant and colorful that she couldn't resist flying over to check it out. As she landed on the flower, she didn't notice the spider hiding nearby. The spider quickly spun a web around the bee, trapping her.

The bee was very scared and didn't know what to do. She wished she had listened to her friends and stayed close to the hive. Sadly, the bee never made it back to her home and her friends never saw her again. The moral of the story is to always be careful when exploring and to stay close to those who love and care for you.

Hannah happily agreed. She said, "Of course, but you need to get your own license first!"

Carl replied, "That's ok, I'll get one and then we can zip together!"

So Carl and Hannah got their licenses and from then on they zip around together, having so much fun!

Later that day, a wise old owl flew by and saw the little rabbit lying on the ground. The owl knew that the rabbit had tried to climb the big, thick tree and had fallen. The owl shook his head sadly and said, "Sometimes, even when we have the power to do something, we need to be careful and take small steps."

Timmy didn't know what to do. He was thirsty and restless, and he didn't want to go back to his room. But then he had an idea. He could ask his mom to take him to the store to get more water. Timmy was happy again because he found a solution to his problem.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a teddy bear named Ted. One night, Lily heard an alarm go off. She was scared because she didn't know what it was for. She asked Ted, "Do you hear that noise too?" Ted nodded his head yes.

Lily got out of bed and walked to her parents' room. She said, "Mommy, Daddy, do you hear the alarm?" Her parents woke up and listened. They didn't know what it was for either. Then, they all heard a knock at the door. It was their neighbor. She said, "There's a fire in the unknown building next door. We need to leave now."

Lily and her family quickly got dressed and left their house. They saw the fire and were glad they were safe. Lily held onto Ted tightly and said, "I'm glad we're together and safe." Ted nodded his head in agreement.

Then, they met a sly fox who told them, "I saw your acorn. It is under that big rock." But the fox was not telling the truth. He wanted the acorn for himself. Sam and the bird believed the fox and went to the big rock. When they moved the rock, they found nothing. The fox had lied to them.

One day, Tweetie met a kind owl named Hoot. Hoot was very wise and knew how to help Tweetie. Hoot told Tweetie to practice flying on the ground. Tweetie tried and tried, and soon got better. Hoot said, "You have improved so much! Now, let's try flying in the gentle wind." Tweetie was scared, but Hoot encouraged her. "You can do it!" Hoot said.

So, Tweetie flew in the gentle wind and it was fun! Tweetie was so happy that she had improved her flying. From that day on, Tweetie was no longer scared of the wind. She would fly up high and see the world, and even play in the gentle wind.

Nemo soon realized that it was not nice to be foolish and quarrel with his friend. He swam to find Dory and apologized. They made up and became friends again. Nemo learned that sharing is important and it's better to have friends than to be foolish and quarrel.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. His tail was enormous! One day, the elephant met a little mouse. The mouse said, "Hello, Mr. Elephant! Why is your tail so big?" The elephant shrugged and said, "I don't know. It has always been big." 

The mouse looked at the elephant's tail and said, "Wow! It's so big that I could hide behind it!" The elephant smiled and said, "Yes, it is big, but it helps me balance when I walk." 

The mouse was amazed and said, "That's so cool! I wish I had a tail like yours." The elephant chuckled and said, "Well, you don't need a tail to be special. You are special just the way you are." The mouse smiled and said, "Thank you, Mr. Elephant. You are very kind." And they became good friends.

He started to run away, but the ball was stuck to his paw. Max tried to shake it off, but the ball wouldn't come off. Then, he felt a tear in his paw.

Lily quickly came to Max's side and saw the ball stuck to his paw. She carefully removed the ball and put some salt on Max's paw to help it heal. Max felt better and was able to continue playing on the beach. From that day on, Max was more careful when playing with unfamiliar objects.

One day, they see a big hill behind their yard. It is new and has smoke coming out. They are curious and want to see it. They ask their mom if they can go. Their mom says no. She says it is a volcano and it is dangerous. She says they have to stay away from it.

But Lila and Ben are ignorant. They do not know what a volcano is. They think it is just a big hill. They think it is a good place to hide and seek. They wait for their mom to go inside. Then they sneak out and run to the volcano.

They start to play hide and seek. Lila hides behind a rock. Ben counts to ten and looks for her. He sees the smoke and hears a loud noise. He thinks it is Lila making a joke. He laughs and runs to the rock. But when he gets there, he does not see Lila. He sees a big hole with fire and lava. He is scared and screams.

Lila hears Ben scream. She comes out from behind the rock. She sees the fire and lava too. She is scared and screams. They run back to their yard. They see their mom coming out. She is angry and worried. She hugs them and scolds them. She tells them they are ignorant and naughty. She tells them they could have been hurt by the volcano. She tells them they have to listen to her and never go there again.

Lila and Ben are sorry and ashamed. They say they are sorry and they will never go there again. They say they did not know what a volcano is. They ask their mom to tell them more about it. Their mom calms down and tells them more about it. She tells them it is a mountain that can erupt and spit out fire and rocks. She tells them it is very hot and dangerous. She tells them some people live near volcanoes and have to be careful. She tells them some volcanoes are asleep and some are awake.

Lila and Ben learn a new word and a new thing. They are not ignorant anymore. They are still curious and want to see more things. But they also know they have to be safe and smart. They do not play hide and seek near the volcano anymore. They play in their yard and have fun. They love their mom and their mom loves them.

Ben and Mia like to go to the beach with Mom and Dad. They play in the sand and splash in the water. Sometimes they see fish and crabs and shells. One day, they see something new. It is pink and long and has many legs. It is a shrimp.

"Look, Mia, a shrimp!" Ben says. He wants to catch it. He runs after it in the water. But the shrimp is fast. It swims away from Ben. Ben tries to pull it with his hand, but he misses. The shrimp is too fast for him.

"Let me try, Ben," Mia says. She is older than Ben. She thinks she can catch the shrimp. She runs after it in the water. But the shrimp is fast. It swims away from Mia. Mia tries to pull it with her hand, but she misses. The shrimp is too fast for her.

"Maybe we can use a net," Ben says. He sees a net on the sand. It belongs to a fisherman. Ben picks up the net and runs to the water. He sees the shrimp. He throws the net over the shrimp. He thinks he has caught it. He pulls the net.

But the net is empty. The shrimp is gone. It has swum under the net. The shrimp is too fast for the net.

"Wow, that shrimp is fast," Mia says. She and Ben look at the water. They see the shrimp swimming away. It looks happy and free.

"Maybe we should let it go," Ben says. He and Mia smile. They like the shrimp. They do not want to hurt it.

"Bye, shrimp," they say. They wave to the shrimp. The shrimp waves back with its legs. Then it swims away. Ben and Mia go back to the sand. They play with their toys. They have fun at the beach.

Lily and Ben are playing with blocks. They want to make a big tower. They have many blocks of different colors. Lily likes pink blocks the best. Ben likes blue blocks the best.

"Can you pass me a pink block, please?" Lily asks Ben. She wants to put a pink block on top of the tower.

"Here you go," Ben says. He gives Lily a pink block. He looks for a blue block for himself.

They keep adding blocks to the tower. It gets taller and taller. They are happy and proud.

But then, Max comes along. Max is a big boy. He likes to break things. He sees the tower and smiles. He has a rod in his hand. It is a long and hard stick.

"Watch out!" Max says. He swings the rod at the tower. He wants to knock it down.

Lily and Ben scream. They try to stop Max. But they are too late. The rod hits the tower. The blocks fall down. The tower is gone.

Lily and Ben are sad and angry. They cry and shout at Max.

"Why did you do that?" Lily asks. "That was our tower. We worked hard on it."

"Yeah, that was not nice," Ben says. "You are mean and rude."

Max laughs. He does not care. He likes to make trouble. He runs away with the rod.

Lily and Ben hug each other. They pick up the blocks. They decide to make another tower. They hope Max will not come back. They still like pink and blue blocks.

Sara was a baby who liked to sleep in her crib. She had a big window in her room, and every morning she saw the sun shine on her toys and books. She smiled and laughed when she saw the bright colors and shapes.

One day, Sara's mommy came to wake her up. She said, "Good morning, my healthy baby. Do you want to go outside and play?" Sara nodded and clapped her hands. She loved to play outside with her mommy and daddy.

Mommy took Sara out of her crib and put her in a stroller. She pushed her along the sidewalk, past the flowers and the birds and the cars. Sara saw many things that made her happy. She pointed and said, "Look, mommy, look!"

But mommy did not look. She was busy talking on her phone. She did not see the big truck that was coming fast. She did not hear the horn that was honking loud. She did not stop at the crosswalk that was red.

The truck hit the stroller and Sara flew out. She landed on the pavement, hard. She felt a lot of pain. She cried and cried, but mommy did not hear her. Mommy was lying on the ground, too. She was not moving. She was not talking.

Sara was alone and scared. She wanted her mommy and daddy. She wanted her crib and her toys and her books. She wanted the sun to shine on her again. But the sun was hidden by the clouds. And Sara was cold and dark.

Mom says yes, but she is very busy. She has a lot of work to do. She tells Lily and Ben to do some things for the party. She gives them a list.

Lily and Ben look at the list. It says: make a cake, blow up balloons, wrap gifts, make cards, and clean the room. Lily and Ben think that is a lot of things. They start to do them.

Lily likes to be bossy. She tells Ben what to do. She says: you make the cake, I will blow up the balloons. You wrap the gifts, I will make the cards. You clean the room, I will do nothing.

Ben does not like to be bossy. He wants to do some things too. He says: no, Lily, that is not fair. We have to share the things. We have to work together. We have to have fun.

Lily and Ben argue. They do not work together. They do not have fun. They make a mess. The cake is burnt, the balloons are popped, the gifts are torn, the cards are scribbled, and the room is dirty.

Mom comes back. She sees the mess. She is not happy. She says: Lily and Ben, what have you done? This is not a party. This is a disaster. You have to fix this. You have to say sorry. You have to be nice.

Lily and Ben feel bad. They say sorry to Mom. They say sorry to each other. They hug. They decide to work together. They fix the mess. They make a new cake, blow up new balloons, wrap new gifts, make new cards, and clean the room.

Mom sees the change. She is happy. She says: Lily and Ben, you have done a great job. You have been nice. You have been a team. You are ready for the party. You can celebrate with your friends.

Lily and Ben smile. They thank Mom. They invite their friends. They have a party. They have fun. They celebrate their birthday. They are happy.

Anna and Ben are playing in the kitchen. They have a big ball that can bounce very high. They take turns to throw the ball and catch it.

"Look, Anna, I can bounce the ball to the ceiling!" Ben says. He throws the ball hard and it hits the ceiling with a loud bang.

"Wow, Ben, that was high!" Anna says. She claps her hands and waits for the ball to come down. But the ball does not come down. It goes into the cupboard above the sink.

"Oh no, where is the ball?" Ben says. He runs to the cupboard and tries to open it. But the cupboard is too high for him. He cannot reach it.

"Maybe we can use a chair," Anna says. She finds a chair and pushes it to the cupboard. She climbs on the chair and opens the cupboard. She sees the ball inside, next to some plates and cups.

"Here it is!" Anna says. She grabs the ball and throws it to Ben. But she throws it too hard and it hits a cup. The cup falls out of the cupboard and breaks on the floor.

"Uh oh, we broke a cup!" Ben says. He hears his mom coming from the living room.

"Anna, Ben, what was that noise?" Mom says. She sees the broken cup and the ball on the floor. She is not happy.

"Sorry, Mom, we were playing with the ball and it bounced into the cupboard and then we broke a cup," Anna says.

"You should not play with the ball in the kitchen. It is dangerous. And you should not climb on the chair. You could fall and hurt yourself," Mom says. She picks up the ball and the broken cup and puts them away. She gives Anna and Ben a long hug.

"I love you, but you have to be careful. Next time, play with the ball outside or in your room. And ask me for help if you need something from the cupboard," Mom says.

"Okay, Mom, we are sorry," Anna and Ben say. They hug Mom back and say they love her too. They go to their room and find another toy to play with.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to watch films on the big TV. Today, they want to watch a film about animals. Anna has a film with lions and zebras. Ben has a film with penguins and seals. They both think their film is the best.

"Let's watch my film first," Anna says. "It has big cats and stripes."

"No, let's watch my film first," Ben says. "It has funny birds and snow."

They start to argue. They do not want to share the TV. They are impatient. They want to watch their film now.

Mom hears them. She comes to the living room. She sees the two films on the floor. She sees Anna and Ben with angry faces.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks. "Why are you not sharing the TV?"

Anna and Ben tell Mom about their films. They both want to watch their film first. They do not want to wait.

Mom shakes her head. She is not happy. She has an idea.

"How about this?" Mom says. "We can watch both films. But we have to take turns. Anna can watch her film first. Then Ben can watch his film. And we can all enjoy the films together. How does that sound?"

Anna and Ben think about it. They do not like to wait. But they also do not like to fight. They want to make Mom happy. They want to be good friends.

"OK, Mom," Anna says. "We can take turns."

"OK, Mom," Ben says. "We can share the TV."

Mom smiles. She is proud of Anna and Ben. She puts Anna's film in the TV. They all sit on the couch. They watch the film about lions and zebras. They see the big cats roar and the stripes run. They learn new things. They have fun.

When the film is over, Mom puts Ben's film in the TV. They watch the film about penguins and seals. They see the funny birds slide and the snow melt. They learn new things. They have fun.

Anna and Ben are happy. They watch both films. They share the TV. They are good friends. They hug Mom. They thank her for the films.

Mom hugs them back. She is happy too. She says, "You're welcome, my loves. Sharing is caring. And watching films is fun."

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and eat snacks. One day, they find a big bag of gummy bears in the kitchen. They are happy and want to share them.

"Look, Ben, gummy bears!" Lily says. "They are my favorite. What color do you like?"

"I like green," Ben says. "They are sour and yummy. What about you?"

"I like red," Lily says. "They are sweet and chewy. Red is the best color."

They start to eat the gummy bears. They each take a handful of their favorite color. They chew and smile.

But then, they see that there are only yellow gummy bears left in the bag. They both stop chewing and frown.

"Yuck, yellow gummy bears," Lily says. "They are bad. They taste like lemon. I don't like lemon."

"Me neither," Ben says. "They are too bitter. I don't want them."

They look at each other. They have a problem. They want more gummy bears, but they don't like the yellow ones.

"What should we do?" Lily asks.

Ben thinks for a moment. He has an idea.

"Maybe we can trade them," he says. "Maybe someone else likes yellow gummy bears. Maybe they have a different opinion."

Lily nods. She thinks it is a good idea.

"Let's go and ask," she says.

"Hi, do you like gummy bears?" Ben asks.

"Yes, we do," the kids say.

"Do you like yellow gummy bears?" Lily asks.

"Yes, we do," the kids say. "They are our favorite. They are bright and tangy. Yellow is the best color."

Lily and Ben are surprised. They didn't know that some people like yellow gummy bears. They have a different opinion.

"Wow, really?" Ben says.

"Yes, really," the kids say.

"Do you want to trade?" Lily asks.

"Yes, we do," the kids say. "What do you have?"

"We have red and green gummy bears," Ben says. "They are popular. They are sweet and sour. Red and green are the best colors."

The kids are excited. They didn't know that some people like red and green gummy bears. They have a different opinion.

"Wow, really?" the kids say.

"Yes, really," Lily and Ben say.

They decide to trade. They give the yellow gummy bears to the kids, and the kids give the red and green gummy bears to Lily and Ben. They are all happy and thank each other.

They start to eat the gummy bears. They each take a handful of their new color. They chew and smile.

They learn that different people have different opinions. They learn that it is okay to like different things. They learn that it is fun to share and trade. They learn that gummy bears are delicious.

Tom nodded. He did not want to get hurt or sick. He wanted to see the flower closer, but he did not touch it.

They heard a moo from the barn. They turned and saw a cow looking at them. The cow was brown and white and had big horns.

"Hi, cow!" Lily said. "Do you like the flower too?"

The cow mooed again and walked towards them. Lily and Tom smiled. They liked the cow. She was friendly and gave them milk.

"Hey, cow, no!" Tom said. "That was our flower. You ate it!"

Lily gasped. She felt sad. She liked the flower. She wanted to see it again.

"Don't worry, my loves," Mom said. "There are many more flowers in the garden. They will bloom soon. You can see them and smell them, but be careful not to touch them. And watch out for the cow. She likes to eat flowers."

"Are you sure?" Mom said. "The kayak is not easy. You have to paddle and balance. And the water is deep and cold."

Lila was a girl who liked to play in the garden. She liked to dig and plant and water the flowers. One day, she found a big, old pumpkin in a corner of the garden. It was round and orange and had a long stem.

Lila wondered what was inside the pumpkin. She took a knife from the kitchen and cut a hole in the pumpkin. She looked inside and saw a lot of seeds and pulp. It smelled bad and was wet and mushy. Lila said, "Yuck! This pumpkin is rotting!"

She threw the knife away and ran to the house. She told her mom what she had found. Her mom said, "That pumpkin is very old, Lila. It was left over from Halloween. Do you know what Halloween is?"

Lila shook her head. She did not know what Halloween was. Her mom said, "Halloween is a fun day when people dress up and go trick-or-treating. They knock on doors and say 'trick or treat' and get candy. Some people also carve pumpkins and make them into lanterns. They cut out eyes and a mouth and put a candle inside. They look scary and funny at night."

Lila said, "That sounds fun! Can we do that next Halloween?" Her mom said, "Sure, we can. But we need a fresh pumpkin, not an old one. An old one will rot and smell and attract bugs. We can go to the farm and pick a new one when it is time."

Lila said, "OK, mom. But can I keep the old pumpkin for now? I want to make something with it." Her mom said, "What do you want to make, Lila?" Lila said, "I want to make a prince!"

Her mom smiled and said, "A prince? How will you do that?" Lila said, "I will use a magic wand and say 'abracadabra' and the pumpkin will turn into a prince. Then he will be my friend and we will play together."

Her mom said, "That sounds like a nice idea, Lila. But you know that magic is not real, right? It is only pretend. The pumpkin will not really turn into a prince. It will just stay a pumpkin."

Lila said, "I know, mom. But I can pretend. It is fun to pretend. Maybe the pumpkin will pretend too. Maybe he will be happy to be a prince and not a rotting pumpkin."

Her mom said, "OK, Lila. You can keep the pumpkin and pretend. But don't forget to wash your hands after you touch it. And don't let it make a mess in the garden. And don't be sad if it falls apart. It is just an old pumpkin, not a real prince."

Lila said, "OK, mom. I will remember. Thank you for letting me keep the pumpkin. I will be nice to him and he will be nice to me. He will be the best prince ever!"

Lila ran back to the garden with a stick in her hand. She said it was her magic wand. She waved it over the pumpkin and said, "Abracadabra! You are a prince now! Hello, prince! What is your name?"

The pumpkin did not answer. It did not move. It did not change. It was still a pumpkin. But Lila did not mind. She smiled and said, "Your name is Prince Pumpkin. You are my friend. Let's play!"

His friends were happy and excited. They all went to the party and had a great time. They played games, ate yummy food, and danced. Timmy felt proud that he had found the invitation and shared it with his friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk in the woods. He saw a big pine tree. It was a hot day, so he sat under the tree to rest. As he sat, he heard a tiny voice.

"Hello!" said a small bug. "I am Ben, the bug. Can you help me? I am lost."

Tim smiled and said, "Yes, I can help you. I will lead you to your home."

So Tim and Ben walked together. Tim led Ben through the woods. They saw other trees and animals. After a while, they found Ben's home under a small rock.

"Thank you for your help," said Ben. Tim waved goodbye and went back to his own home. He felt happy to have helped his new friend.

Timmy felt sad for the tiger and wanted to help. He asked his mom for some bandages and wrapped up the tiger's leg. The tiger was so happy and thanked Timmy.

"Now I can hop again!" said the tiger, happily. Timmy was happy too, knowing he had helped the tiger. From that day on, the tiger and Timmy were the best of friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go on walks with her mommy and daddy. One day, they saw a sign that said "Keep off the grass". Lily asked her parents what the sign meant, and they explained that it meant they should not walk on the grass.

As they continued their walk, they saw a lonely bird sitting on a branch. Lily wanted to help the bird, so she tried to push it off the branch to play with it. But her parents stopped her and explained that pushing the bird could hurt it.

Lily learned that it's important to read signs and not push things that could get hurt. She also learned that it's important to be kind to animals and not make them feel lonely. From then on, Lily always made sure to read signs and be gentle with the creatures she met on her walks.

Once upon a time, there was a goose named Gigi. Gigi lived in a big pond with her friends. One day, Gigi went for a walk and found a soft pillow. She lay down on it and felt very comfortable. 

Her friend, a little duck named Ducky, saw her lying on the pillow and asked, "Gigi, where did you find that pillow?" 

Gigi replied, "I found it over there by the tree. It's very comfortable. You should try it too!" 

Ducky went to the tree and found the pillow. She lay down on it and said, "Wow, Gigi! You were right. This pillow is very comfortable. Thank you for telling me about it." 

From that day on, Gigi and Ducky would often lie on the pillow together and talk about their day. They were happy to have found something so comfortable to rest on.

"Look, Chirp! I found a funny feather!" Tweet said.

Chirp looked at the feather and said, "That feather looks like it came from the big bird who lives on the other side of the forest. Be careful, Tweet!"

Tweet didn't listen and decided to fly over to the big bird's nest. As he got closer, the big bird woke up and started to rock the nest. Tweet got scared and dropped the feather. He quickly flew away and went back to his friends.

"I won't go near the big bird's nest again," Tweet said to Chirp. "Thanks for warning me!"

From that day on, Tweet and Chirp played together and had fun without getting into any more trouble.

Charlie had a bow and arrow. It was dark brown and very furry. He went to the forest to practice shooting arrows. 

As he was practicing, he found a funny label on a tree. He went over to it and read the label. It said "Do Not Touch". 

Charlie looked around but nobody was there. He thought it would be okay to touch it. He gingerly touched the label and suddenly a big cloud of smoke appeared!

"Whoa," said Charlie and he jumped back. Out of the cloud of smoke, a fairy appeared. She was wearing a sparkly dress and had wings like a butterfly.

"What did you do?" said the fairy. 

Charlie bowed his head and said, "I'm sorry. I didn't mean it." 

The fairy smiled and waved her wand. "It's alright", she said. "But from now on, please don't touch labels without asking first!" 

Charlie nodded and understood. He thanked the fairy and promised not to touch any labels without asking. Then the fairy flew away in a puff of smoke. 

Charlie put his bow and arrow back in his bag and went home, remembering the fairy's words: "Don't touch the labels!"

Max felt jealous of Lily's toy and wanted it for himself. But when he saw how sad Lily was, he felt bad for stealing it. He went to Lily and said, "I'm sorry I took your toy. I was jealous. Can we still be friends?" Lily forgave Max and they continued to play together. From that day on, Max learned that stealing was not the right thing to do and that it's important to be kind to others.

Lily felt very happy and proud. Even though she didn't find the treasure she was looking for, she found something even better - the joy of watching someone else do something amazing. From then on, Lily loved to applaud and cheer for others who did brave and cool things.

Once upon a time, there was a little ant named Andy. Andy was walking around when he saw a big, bright light. He went closer to see what it was and found a glowing light bulb.

"Wow, this is so cool!" said Andy.

Suddenly, a little girl came and saw Andy near the light bulb. She got very angry and said, "You shouldn't be here, you little ant! You broke my light bulb and now I'm very guilty for shouting at you."

Andy tried to explain that he didn't break the light bulb, but the little girl didn't believe him. She squished him with her foot and poor Andy died.

The little girl felt very guilty for what she had done, but it was too late. Andy was gone forever.

Once upon a time, there was a great giant. He was very big and strong. He lived on top of a big hill. One day, he met a little boy named Timmy.

"Hello, little boy. What brings you to my hill?" asked the giant.

"I want to play with you," said Timmy.

The giant smiled and said, "Sure, we can play together. But be careful, I might melt if it gets too hot."

Timmy didn't understand what the giant meant, but he nodded and they started playing. They played hide and seek, tag, and even had a picnic. But then, the sun started to get really hot.

"I'm starting to feel funny," said the giant.

"What's wrong?" asked Timmy.

"I think I'm melting," said the giant.

Timmy didn't know what to do, but he didn't want the giant to melt. So he grabbed a bucket of water and poured it on the giant. The water cooled him down and he stopped melting.

"Thank you, Timmy. You saved me," said the giant.

From that day on, the giant and Timmy became great friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl named Hootie. Hootie lived in a big tree in the forest. One day, Hootie was talking to his friend, a little mouse named Squeaky.

Squeaky said, "Hootie, why do you always sneeze in the spring season?"

Hootie replied, "I sneeze because the flowers make me sneeze. But I love the spring season because everything is so colorful and beautiful."

Squeaky said, "I love the spring season too, but I don't sneeze like you do."

Hootie chuckled and said, "That's because you are a mouse and I am an owl. We are different, but we can still be friends."

Squeaky smiled and said, "You are a wise owl, Hootie."

And Hootie replied, "Thank you, Squeaky. You are a good friend."

His friend, Sarah, said, "Be careful! Crocodiles are dangerous. They can bite you and hurt you."

Timmy replied, "I know, but I want to see it up close."

As Timmy got closer to the river, he noticed that the crocodile was not moving. It was just lying there, not even blinking. Timmy said, "What's wrong with the crocodile? Why isn't it moving?"

Sarah said, "I think it's dead. It must have rotted in the sun for too long."

Timmy felt sad for the crocodile. He said, "We should bury it and give it a proper goodbye."

So, Timmy and Sarah dug a hole and buried the crocodile. They said a little prayer for it and promised to always respect the animals in the jungle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to pick vegetables from her garden. "Hello, little butterfly!" Lily said. "What are you doing here?"

"I'm just passing through," the butterfly replied. "But I couldn't help but notice how beautiful your garden is. Those vegetables look delicious!"

Lily smiled. "Thank you! Would you like to try one?"

The raven was happy and grateful for the little girl's kindness. But one day, the little girl forgot to close the window and the raven flew away. The little girl was sad and missed the raven, but she knew that it was free to fly wherever it wanted to.

From that day on, the little girl always remembered to close the window and take care of the animals that needed help.

Once upon a time, there was a king who wore a shiny crown. He was very famous and people from all over the land came to see him. One day, a little girl came up to the king and said, "Can I try on your crown?" The king smiled and said, "Of course you can!" 

The little girl put on the crown and started to shake her head back and forth. The crown fell off and rolled away. The little girl felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to break it." The king picked up the crown and said, "Don't worry, it's just a crown. You can always make a new one."

The little girl was happy again and said, "I want to be famous like you one day." The king smiled and said, "You don't need to be famous to be special. Just be yourself and always try your best." The little girl nodded and said, "Okay, I will remember that." And from that day on, the little girl always remembered the king's words and tried her best in everything she did.
